Every 30 minutes if weather conditions are below those for VFR; otherwise hourly
Only when the ceiling and/or visibility changes by a reportable value
Air Traffic Services.explanation: ATIS broadcasts are updated immediately upon receipt of official meteorological reports regardless of content changes.

Air Traffic Services.question: Flight Information Service shall be provided to aircraft in order to avoid collision hazards when operating in airspace classes:
options: C, D, E, F and G
A, B, C, D, E, F and G
Air Traffic Services.explanation: Flight Information Service regarding collision hazards is provided in airspace classes C, D, E, F, and G.

Air Traffic Services.question: The lateral limit of CTR shall extend to at least ____ NMs from the center of aerodrome in directions from where approaches may be made:
Air Traffic Services.explanation: The lateral boundary of a Control Zone must extend at least 5 NM from the aerodrome center in approach directions.

Air Traffic Services.question: At radio communications, "Distress" differs from "Urgency" because in the first case
options: The aeroplane has suffered damages which impair its fitness to fly
There is a serious and imminent danger requiring immediate assistance
The aeroplane will not be able to reach a suitable aerodrome
Air Traffic Services.explanation: Distress represents a condition of being threatened by grave and imminent danger requiring immediate assistance.

Air Traffic Services.question: The Alerting Service is provided by:
options: The ATS unit responsible for the aircraft at that moment
Air Traffic Services.explanation: Alerting service is provided by whichever ATS unit is responsible for the aircraft at that moment.

Air Traffic Services.question: The phases related to an aircraft in emergency or believed in emergency are:
options: Uncertainty phase, distress phase, urgency phase
Uncertainty phase, alert phase, distress phase
Uncertainty phase, urgency phase, distress phase
Air Traffic Services.explanation: The three emergency phases in sequence are Uncertainty phase (INCERFA), Alert phase (ALERFA), and Distress phase (DETRESFA).

Air Traffic Services.question: When an aircraft is experiencing difficulties, triggering of the alert phase is responsibility of
options: Air traffic control and flight information centers
Air Traffic Services.explanation: Triggering emergency phases like the Alert phase is the responsibility of Air Traffic Control and Flight Information Centers.

Air Traffic Services.question: What type of flight is allowed in class A airspace
Air Traffic Services.explanation: Class A airspace strictly permits IFR flights only.

Air Traffic Services.question: Alert phase is defined as follows:
options: A situation where an apprehension exists as to the safety of an aircraft and its occupants
An emergency event in which an aircraft and its occupants are considered to be threatened by a danger
A situation related to an aircraft and its occupants are considered to be in a state of emergency
Air Traffic Services.explanation: Alert Phase (ALERFA) is a situation where apprehension exists as to the safety of an aircraft and its occupants.

Air Traffic Services.question: A situation in which apprehension exists as to the safety of an aircraft. To which emergency phase does this situation correspond?
Air Traffic Services.explanation: Apprehension regarding aircraft safety corresponds to ALERFA.

Air Traffic Services.question: Which of the following signals is a distress signal?
options: In radiotelephony the spoken words PAN, PAN
A parachute flare showing a red light
The repeated switching on and off of the navigation lights
Air Traffic Services.explanation: A pyrotechnic red parachute flare signal indicates Distress.

Air Traffic Services.question: An aircraft is in emergency when:
options: It is threatened by grave danger
It is threatened by grave danger and requires immediate assistance
Air Traffic Services.explanation: An emergency condition means the aircraft is threatened by grave danger and requires immediate assistance.

Air Traffic Services.question: The different emergency phases (in correct order) are:
Air Traffic Services.explanation: The three emergency phases in order are INCERFA, ALERFA, DETRESFA.

Air Traffic Services.question: Which of the following statements describes the Alert Phase (ALERFA)?
options: An aircraft fails to arrive within 30 minutes of the ETA which was last notified to ATC.
An aircraft declares that the fuel remaining is insufficient to reach safety.
An aircraft which has been cleared to land fails to land within 5 minutes of the ETA and communication has not been re-established.
Air Traffic Services.explanation: When an aircraft cleared to land fails to land within 5 minutes of ETA without radio contact, ALERFA is declared.

Air Traffic Services.question: DETRESFA is where:
options: An aircraft fails to land within 5 minutes of being cleared to land
The fuel on board is considered to be exhausted
Air Traffic Services.explanation: DETRESFA (Distress Phase) is declared when fuel on board is calculated to be exhausted or insufficient.

Air Traffic Services.question: RSP 180 indicates:
options: Time in seconds taken by a pilot to receive surveillance instructions from the controller.
Time in seconds between flight crew/HMI and controller/HMI.
Distance in NMS between two way points in defined RSP airspace.
Air Traffic Services.explanation: RSP 180 specifies maximum delivery time performance in seconds between human-machine interfaces.

Air Traffic Services.question: A strayed aircraft is an aircraft:
options: that has deviated significantly from its intended track or reports that it is lost.
that has been observed or is reported to be operating in a given area but whose identity has not been established.
only that aircraft which has deviated significantly its intended track.
Air Traffic Services.explanation: A strayed aircraft is defined as an aircraft that has deviated significantly from track or reports lost.

Air Traffic Services.question: Having filed a flight plan to a particular destination and having landed at another destination, you should notify ATC:
options: within 60 minutes after landing at the alternate destination
within 30 minutes after landing at the alternate destination
within 30 minutes of your intended ETA at your original destination.
Air Traffic Services.explanation: If landing elsewhere, ATC must be notified within 30 minutes of the original destination's ETA.

Air Traffic Services.question: Designated airspace within controlled airspace in India is classified as Class:
Air Traffic Services.explanation: Controlled airspace in India below FL 290 is primarily designated as Class C and Class D.

Air Traffic Services.question: TSA801(A) is an airspace:
options: temporarily segregated and allocated in Delhi FIR
temporarily segregated and allocated in Chennai FIR
denoting an area navigation route in India
Air Traffic Services.explanation: TSA801(A) is a Temporarily Segregated Area located in Chennai FIR.

Air Traffic Services.question: Temporary Reserved Area (TRA) is an airspace temporarily reserved allocated:
options: through which other traffic may be allowed to transit in VMC only
through which other traffic is not allowed to transit with out proper equipment
through which other traffic may be allowed to transit under ATC clearance
Air Traffic Services.explanation: Traffic may transit a TRA provided they receive ATC clearance.

Air Traffic Services.question: MFA published in AIP ensures at least 1000 feet vertical clearance from obstacles within ____ of center line?
Air Traffic Services.explanation: Minimum Flight Altitude (MFA) in Indian AIP provides 1,000 ft obstacle clearance within 10 km of route centerline.

Air Traffic Services.question: Class C airspaces in India extend from
Air Traffic Services.explanation: Class C airspaces in India extend vertically from 4,000 ft up to FL 285.

Air Traffic Services.question: After rain Controller reports that runway is WET. That indicates to a pilot that
options: the surface is soaked but there is no standing water.
there is no standing water with a depth of more than 3 cms on one third of the runway.
the runway is closed due water logging and pilot should divert.
Air Traffic Services.explanation: A WET runway report indicates the surface is soaked with moisture without standing water.

Air Traffic Services.question: In AIP, Enroute 3.1, ATS routes are described as::
Air Traffic Services.explanation: Section ENR 3.1 of the Indian AIP covers Conventional Navigation Routes.

Air Traffic Services.question: In AIP, Enroute 3.2, ATS routes are described as:
Air Traffic Services.explanation: Section ENR 3.2 of the AIP covers Area Navigation (RNAV) Routes.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: An aircraft is maintaining FL 150 within airspace class D. Another aircraft below at FL 140 is receiving a clearance to descend to FL 70. It is severe turbulence in the area. When is the earliest that a clearance to descend to FL 140 or below can be expected?
options: When the other aircraft has reported that it has left FL 140.
When the other aircraft has reported that it has reached FL 70.
When the other aircraft has reported that it has descended through FL 130.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Due to severe turbulence, vertical separation must be maintained until the preceding aircraft reports reaching or passing through a level that provides standard vertical clearance (at least 1,000 ft below FL 140, which is FL 130).

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: The longitudinal separation minima between aircraft departed from the same aerodrome and following the same track, and the preceding aircraft is maintaining a true airspeed of 20kt or more faster than the succeeding aircraft, is:
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Standard departure longitudinal separation is reduced to 5 minutes if the preceding aircraft is at least 20 knots faster than the succeeding aircraft.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: The longitudinal separation minima based on time between aircraft at same cruising level where navigation aids permit frequent determination of position and speed and the preceding aircraft is maintaining a true airspeed of 40kt or more faster than the succeeding aircraft, is:
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: When the preceding aircraft maintains a TAS at least 40 knots faster than the following aircraft, the required en-route longitudinal time separation is reduced to 3 minutes.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: The longitudinal separation minima based on time between aircraft at same cruising level where navigation aids permit frequent determination of position and speed and the preceding aircraft is maintaining a true airspeed of 20kt or more faster than the succeeding aircraft, is:
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: A 5-minute longitudinal separation interval applies when the leading aircraft is maintaining a TAS at least 20 knots faster than the following aircraft.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: The longitudinal separation minima based on time between aircraft at same cruising level where navigation aids permit frequent determination of position and speed, is:
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Standard time-based longitudinal separation for aircraft at the same cruising level on the same track with frequent position checks is 10 minutes.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: The longitudinal separation minima between aircraft departed from same aerodrome and following the same track, and the preceding aircraft maintaining a true airspeed of 40kt or more faster than the succeeding aircraft is:
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Departure longitudinal separation is 3 minutes between aircraft departing from the same aerodrome on the same track if the preceding aircraft is 40 kt or faster.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: The longitudinal separation minima based on distance using DME, and aircraft "on track" uses DME stations, is:
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Standard DME distance-based longitudinal separation for aircraft on the same track using co-located/on-track DME facilities is 20 NM.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: When an aircraft will pass through the level of another aircraft on the same track, the following minimum longitudinal separation shall be provided:
options: 5 minutes at the time the level is crossed.
15 minutes at the time the level is crossed.
10 minutes at the time the level is crossed.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Standard longitudinal separation while climbing or descending through another aircraft's level on the same track is 15 minutes at the time of level crossing.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: "ESSENTIAL TRAFFIC" is that controlled flight to which the provision of separation by ATC is applicable, but which, in relation to a particular controlled flight is not separated therefrom by the appropriate separation minima. Whenever separation minima is not applied, the following flights are considered essential traffic one to each other:
options: All IFR flights in controlled airspace and controlled VFR
Controlled VFR flights and VFR flights.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Essential traffic information is provided between all controlled flights (all IFR flights in controlled airspace and controlled VFR flights) when required separation minima cannot be maintained.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: Above FL 290 the vertical flight separation between aircraft on the same direction is:
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: In non-RVSM airspace above FL 290, aircraft flying in the same direction require 4,000 ft vertical separation under conventional semi-circular rules.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: Track separation between aircraft using the same NDB shall be applied requiring the aircraft to fly:
options: At least 30° separated at a distance of 15NM or more from the facility.
At least 45° separated at a distance of 15NM or more from the facility.
At least 30° separated at a distance of 15 miles or more from the facility.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Track separation using the same NDB requires tracks to diverge by at least 30 degrees at a distance of 15 NM or more from the aid.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: Two aircraft flying at FL 170 using GNSS are confirmed to be established on tracks separated by 120 degrees with zero offset between two waypoints. At least one aircraft is to be at a minimum distance _____ NMs from a common point for separation.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: GNSS-based lateral/track separation requires at least 15 NM distance from a common point for tracks diverging by 120 degrees.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: If an ATC clearance is not suitable to the pilot in command of an aircraft:
options: He may request another clearance and the ATC concerned has to accept the pilot request.
He may request and, if practicable, obtain an amended clearance.
The pilot has to accept the ATC clearance because it has been based on the flightplan filed with ATC.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: A pilot-in-command who considers an issued ATC clearance unsuitable may request an amended clearance, which ATC will issue if practicable.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: The "VMC and own separation" ATC clearance is used for a controlled flight to cross the level of another controlled flight when:
options: Requested by the pilot in airspace classes A and B and authorised by ATC.
Requested by the pilot, during the day light and authorized by the state overflown.
Requested by the pilot and authorized by the state overflown.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Clearing an aircraft to maintain VMC and its own separation while climbing/descending through another level is allowed during daylight hours if requested by the pilot and authorized by the appropriate ATS authority.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: A/C on same level converging track has separation
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Standard time separation between aircraft on converging tracks at the same cruising level without radar is 15 minutes.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: What are the controlled IFR separation methods applied by ATC?
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: ATC applies vertical separation, horizontal separation (longitudinal and lateral), and composite separation.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: The vertical IFR separation minimum being applied by ATC within a controlled airspace below FL 290 is:
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Standard vertical separation minimum below FL 290 is 1,000 ft (300 m).

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: The vertical IFR separation minimum being applied by ATC within a controlled airspace above FL 290 is:
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: In non-RVSM airspace above FL 290, vertical separation between controlled flights is 2,000 ft (600 m).

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: Longitudinal separation minima based on distance using DME for aircraft at the same cruising level and track, provided that each aircraft utilizes "On Track" DME stations and separation is checked by obtaining simultaneous DME readings, is:
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: 20 NM DME separation applies for aircraft at the same cruising level on the same track using on-track DME stations.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: A "RNAV" distance based separation minimum may be used at the time the level is crossed, provided that each aircraft reports its distance to or from the same "on track" waypoint. This minimum is:
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Standard RNAV distance-based longitudinal separation while passing through levels is 80 NM.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: A VFR flight constitutes essential traffic to other VFR flights, when operating in controlled airspace classified as:
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: In Class B airspace, ATC provides separation between all VFR flights; thus, unseparated VFR traffic constitutes essential traffic to other VFR flights.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: RCP 120 is the number of :
options: Transmissions loaded on aircraft FMS for data link exchange.
Minutes required to divert to a suitable aerodrome under ETOP conditions.
Seconds it takes for an instruction to travel from the ground to aircraft and acknowledgment back to the ground.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: RCP 120 specifies a Required Communication Performance time limit of 120 seconds for end-to-end communication transactions.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: Vertical or horizontal separation shall be provided between:
options: All flights in class A, B and C airspaces.
All flights in class A and B airspaces.
All flights in class B, C and D airspaces.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: ATC provides vertical or horizontal separation between all flights (both IFR and VFR) operating in Class A and Class B airspaces.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: The separation method whereby the vertical and horizontal separation may be reduced till a maximum of half the standard criteria is called:
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Composite separation is a technique combining half of the standard vertical and horizontal separation criteria.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: ADS-B ground station is more than 110 NMS from two aircraft at same level. Only ADS-B is being used for separation in non radar environment. The minimum safe distance between these aircraft is _____ NMs.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: In a non-radar ADS-B environment beyond typical terminal range (over 110 NM), standard procedural ADS-B separation defaults to 10 NM.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: Cruising level IFR during cruise within controlled airspace shall be given as flight level (FL)
options: Above the transition altitude when applicable.
If the obstacle clearance is more than 2000ft.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Cruising levels for IFR flights operating at or above the transition altitude/layer are always expressed in terms of Flight Levels (FL).

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: Aircraft flying along the same track may be separated by DME-distances from the same DME and it is confirmed that the aircraft have passed each other. Specify the shortest difference in DME-distance to make it possible for one aircraft to climb or descend
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: Once aircraft on the same track are positively confirmed by DME to have passed each other, a minimum 10 NM separation allows vertical level change.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: Track separation between aircraft using the same VOR shall be applied requiring the aircraft to fly:
options: At least 15° separated at a distance of 15 miles or more from the facility.
At least 15° separated at a distance of 15NM or more from the facility.
At least 30° separated at a distance of 15NM or more from the facility.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: VOR-based lateral track separation requires tracks to diverge by at least 15 degrees at a distance of 15 NM or more from the facility.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: ATC clearances are solely issued for:
options: Alerting pilots about other aircraft in close vicinity.
Making pilots follow laid down procedures.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: The sole objective of ATC clearances is to expedite and separate air traffic.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: The longitudinal separation minima based on DME, and each aircraft "on track" uses DME stations, is:
options: 10NM provided that the leading aircraft maintains a true airspeed of 40kt or more faster than the succeeding aircraft.
10NM provided that the leading aircraft maintains a true airspeed of 20kt or more faster than the succeeding aircraft.
20NM provided that the leading aircraft maintains a true airspeed of 10kt or more faster than the succeeding aircraft.
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: DME-based longitudinal separation can be reduced to 10 NM provided the preceding aircraft is maintaining a TAS at least 20 knots faster than the succeeding aircraft.

SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.question: FMS/RNAV:
options: Can be used for conventional procedures only if AFM permits
Cannot be used for conventional procedures.
Can be used for conventional procedures if permitted by DGCA
SEPARATION METHODS AND MINIMA.explanation: An FMS/RNAV system can be utilized to fly conventional navigation procedures provided the Airplane Flight Manual (AFM) explicitly approves it.

SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.question: An arriving aircraft is making a straight in approach; a departing aircraft may take off in any direction:
options: Until five minutes before the arriving aircraft is estimated to be over the instrument runway
Until ten minutes before the arriving aircraft is estimated to be over the instrument runway
Until two minutes before the arriving aircraft is estimated to be over instrument runway
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.explanation: When an arriving aircraft is executing a straight-in approach, a departing aircraft may take off in any direction until 5 minutes before the arriving aircraft is estimated to be over the threshold or instrument runway.
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.chapter: Separation in the Vicinity of Aerodromes

SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.question: For controlled traffic that shall be separated in the vicinity of an airport, separation minima may be reduced:
options: At the discretion of the air traffic controller
When the commander in the following aircraft has the preceding aircraft in sight and is able to maintain own separation
If the commander of the involved aircraft so requests
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.explanation: In aerodrome traffic, separation minima can be reduced when the pilot-in-command of a following aircraft reports the preceding aircraft in sight and accepts responsibility for maintaining visual separation.
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.chapter: Separation in the Vicinity of Aerodromes

SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.question: At the commencement of final approach, if the controller possesses wind information in the form of components, significant changes in the mean surface wind direction and speed shall be transmitted to aircraft. The mean headwind/tailwind component significant change is:
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.explanation: Significant changes in wind components, specifically a change in the mean headwind/tailwind component of 2 knots or more, must be passed to the aircraft prior to or at final approach.
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.chapter: Separation in the Vicinity of Aerodromes

SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.question: The EAT (Expected Approach Time) has to be transmitted to the pilot as soon as possible, in case expected delay is:
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.explanation: An Expected Approach Time (EAT) shall be transmitted to the aircraft as soon as practicable whenever an arriving aircraft is expected to be delayed by 5 minutes or more (or as locally specified by ATS).
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.chapter: Separation in the Vicinity of Aerodromes

SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.question: A so called "Visual Approach" can be performed:
options: During VFR flight, there should be a visibility of 5km or more
During IFR flights, if the cloudbase is 1000ft more than the appropriate DA/MDA for that procedure
During IFR flights, if there is permanent sight of the movement area and underlying ground
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.explanation: A visual approach is an approach by an IFR flight when either part or all of the instrument approach procedure is not completed and the approach is executed with visual reference to terrain/ground and movement area.
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.chapter: Separation in the Vicinity of Aerodromes

SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.question: "Timed Approach Procedure" is used as necessary to expedite the approach of a number of arriving aircraft. This will be obtained requesting aircraft:
options: To maintain a specified speed during the approach procedure
To pass the specified point inbound at the previously notified time
To apply a step down descent between aircraft in the approach sequence
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.explanation: In a timed approach procedure, aircraft are given specific approach times to pass a designated fixes/points inbound to sequence aircraft efficiently.
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.chapter: Separation in the Vicinity of Aerodromes

SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.question: During an arrival procedure under an IFR flight plan in VMC conditions, traffic avoidance is the responsibility of:
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.explanation: Regardless of receiving ATC service, when operating under visual meteorological conditions (VMC), ultimate responsibility for see-and-avoid traffic collision prevention rests with the pilot-in-command.
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.chapter: Separation in the Vicinity of Aerodromes

SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.question: If the crew on an arriving aircraft approaching a controlled aerodrome will report "field in sight", a clearance for "visual approach" may be given under certain conditions:
options: The meteorological visibility must not be less than 8km
The approach must be passing the FAF
The air traffic controller will provide separation to other controlled traffic
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.explanation: Issuing a visual approach clearance to an IFR aircraft does not relieve ATC of its obligation to maintain standard separation between that flight and other controlled traffic.
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.chapter: Separation in the Vicinity of Aerodromes

SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.question: Which statement is correct? During a "visual approach" in controlled airspace (class C):
options: ATC will apply separation with other traffic
The pilot has to apply separation with other traffic
ATC will apply separation with other arriving traffic
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.explanation: In Class C airspace, Air Traffic Control maintains separation between all IFR flights (including IFR flights executing a visual approach) and other controlled traffic.
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.chapter: Separation in the Vicinity of Aerodromes

SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.question: One minute separation may be used between departing aircraft if they are to fly on tracks diverging by at least:
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.explanation: Longitudinal departure separation can be reduced to 1 minute if departing aircraft fly tracks that diverge by at least 45 degrees immediately after takeoff.
SEPARATION IN THE VICINITY OF AERODROMES.chapter: Separation in the Vicinity of Aerodromes

PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.question: When instructed by ATC to hold short of Runway pilot should stop:
options: With nose gear on hold line
So that no part of the A/C extends beyond hold line
So that the Flt Deck Area of A/C is even with the hold line
PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.explanation: When holding short of a runway, no part of the aircraft is permitted to extend beyond the holding line to ensure clearance from the runway-in-use.

PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.question: The following aircraft will be given priority to land:
options: An aircraft with VVIP on board
An aircraft with critical shortage of fuel
PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.explanation: An aircraft experiencing an emergency or urgency situation, such as a critical fuel shortage, is given priority over all other traffic including VVIP flights.

PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.question: Apron is an area on aerodrome where following activities take place:
options: Loading/unloading of passengers, mail and cargo only.
Loading/unloading of passengers, mail and cargo, fueling, parking or maintenance.
PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.explanation: An apron is a defined area on a land aerodrome intended to accommodate aircraft for purposes of loading or unloading passengers, mail or cargo, fueling, parking, or maintenance.

PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.question: For safety reasons, a person should remain away from a jet engine by at least:
PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.explanation: To avoid danger from jet blast hazards and suction zones, a minimum safe distance of 200 feet should be maintained.

PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.question: Movement area of an aerodrome constitutes the following:
options: Area including runways / taxiways excluding apron
Area excluding taxiways but including runways and apron
PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.explanation: The movement area is that part of an aerodrome to be used for the take-off, landing, and taxiing of aircraft, consisting of the manoeuvring area and the apron(s).

PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.question: The maneuvering area of an airport is that area:
options: Normally referred to as the ramp or apron.
Used for taxiing, taking off and landing.
Used when taxiing to and from the parking area.
PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.explanation: The manoeuvring area is defined as that part of an aerodrome to be used for the take-off, landing, and taxiing of aircraft, excluding aprons.

PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.question: An Aircraft shall report 'long final' when it is at _____ from the approach end of the rwy:
PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.explanation: 'Long final' is reported when an aircraft is on final approach and is greater than 4 NM (typically around 8 NM) from the threshold.

PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.question: What defines a controlled aerodrome?
options: It must be located within a CTR.
It must have a control tower giving an ATC service.
It must have a control tower and be in a CTR.
PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.explanation: A controlled aerodrome is an aerodrome at which air traffic control service is provided to aerodrome traffic, regardless of whether a control zone (CTR) exists.

PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.question: Aerodrome traffic is considered to be:
options: Aircraft on the movement area and flying in the vicinity.
Aircraft on the manoeuvring area and flying in the vicinity.
Aircraft on the movement area only.
PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.explanation: Aerodrome traffic includes all traffic on the manoeuvring area of an aerodrome and all aircraft flying in the vicinity of an aerodrome.

PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.question: Aircraft shall not be held closer to a runway-in-use:
options: Than at 40m from the runway edge.
PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.explanation: Aircraft must not be held closer to a runway-in-use than at a designated runway-holding position.

PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.question: Friction Co efficient due to snow - in how many segments is runway divided based on friction level:
PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.explanation: For runway condition reporting, the runway is divided into three equal segments (thirds) to assess friction and surface condition.

PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.question: Runway friction coefficient 0.20 means estimated surface friction:
PROCEDURES FOR AERODROME CONTROL SERVICE.explanation: A friction coefficient below 0.25 indicates poor braking action / estimated surface friction.

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: The minimum radar separation to be provided to aircraft established on the localizer course shall be:
options: 2.0NM between aircraft on adjacent localizer course
2.5NM between aircraft on the same localizer course
5.0NM between aircraft on the same localizer course
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: When established on the same localizer course during radar vectoring for ILS approach, the minimum radar separation can be reduced to 2.5 NM under specific conditions.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: Unless otherwise prescribed by the appropriate ATS authority, the horizontal radar separation minimum prescribed by ICAO shall be:
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: The standard horizontal radar separation minimum prescribed by ICAO in terminal and en-route environments is 5.0 NM unless lower minima are approved by local authorities.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: Where ADS-B is used for identification, aircraft may be identified by the following procedure:
options: Asking him to squawk assigned mode A code C.
Direct recognition of the aircraft identification in an ADS-B label.
Recognition of an assigned discrete code, the setting of which has been verified.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: With ADS-B surveillance, aircraft identification can be directly recognized via the callsign transmitted in the ADS-B data label.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: An aircraft is considered to be maintaining its assigned level as long as the SSR mode C derived level information indicated that it is within:
options: +/- 500ft of the assigned level in non RVSM airspace
+/- 200ft of the assigned level in RVSM airspace
+/- 300ft of the assigned level in RVSM airspace
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: An aircraft is considered to be maintaining an assigned level if the pressure-altitude derived level info indicates it is within +/- 200 ft (+/- 60 m) of that level.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: An aircraft in climb or descent is considered to have crossed a level when the SSR mode C derived level information indicates that it has passed this level in the required direction by:
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: For ATC separation purposes, an aircraft is considered to have crossed a level when the Mode C readout shows it has passed the level by more than 300 ft in the required direction.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR) information may be used alone in the provision of separation between aircraft provided:
options: Instructions to pilot are acknowledged by him by making specific maneuver(s).
Aircraft identification is established and maintained by use of discrete SSR codes.
It can not be used for providing separation.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: SSR data alone can be used for separation if positive identification is established and maintained using discrete squawk codes.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: Radar identification of a departing aircraft can be achieved if a radar blip is observed within a certain distance from the end of the runway. Identification has to be achieved within:
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: A departing aircraft can be radar-identified if a target/blip is observed within 1 NM of the end of the runway following departure.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: Separation based on the use of MLAT position symbols and PSR blips shall be applied so that:
options: the distance between the centres of the position symbols and PSR blips, representing the positions of the aircraft concerned, is never less than a prescribed minimum.
the distance between the edges of the position symbols and PSR blips, representing the positions of the aircraft concerned, is never less than a prescribed minimum.
the distance between the furthest edges of the position symbols and PSR blips, representing the positions of the aircraft concerned, is never more than a prescribed minimum.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: Radar/surveillance separation is measured from center-to-center of the targets, symbols, or blips representing aircraft positions.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: The air traffic control unit has reported 'radar contact'. What does that mean to the pilot?
options: The aircraft is subject to positive control
The radar identity of the aircraft has been established
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: 'Radar contact' is used by ATC to inform the pilot that the aircraft has been identified on the radar display.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: When a RADAR operator says the following to an aircraft: 'fly heading 030', the pilot must fly heading:
options: 030° magnetic in still air conditions (thereby flying the magnetic track)
030° true, in still air conditions (thereby flying the true track)
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: Radar vectors given as headings are magnetic headings for the pilot to fly, without applying wind drift corrections unless instructed.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: Which code shall be used on Mode 'A' to provide recognition of an aircraft subjected to unlawful interference?
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: Transponder code 7500 is reserved exclusively to signal unlawful interference (hijacking).
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: Upon intercepting the assigned radial, the controller advises you that you are on the airway and to 'resume own navigation'. This phrase means that:
options: radar services are terminated and you will be responsible for position reports
You are to assume responsibility for your own navigation
You are to contact the center at the next reporting point
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: 'Resume own navigation' instructs the pilot to navigate using onboard instruments along the cleared route rather than following controller vectors.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: What does the ATC term 'radar contact' signify?
options: Your aircraft has been identified on the radar display and radar flight instructions will be provided until radar identification is terminated
You will be given traffic advisories until advised that the service has been terminated or that radar contact has been lost
ATC is receiving your transponder and will furnish vectors and traffic advisories until you are advised that contact has been lost
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: 'Radar contact' indicates that ATC has identified the target on the radar display and will provide surveillance/radar services until advised otherwise.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: Where a 'Secondary Surveillance Radar' (SSR) is not available, radar identification may be achieved by one of the following procedures:
options: To instruct the pilot to execute one or more changes of 10°
To instruct the pilot to execute one or more changes of 45°
To instruct the pilot to execute one or more changes of 30° or more
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: Primary radar identification via vectoring requires observing compliance with an instruction to turn by 30 degrees or more.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: When 'Secondary Radar' is used, an aircraft may be identified by one of the following procedures:
options: To request pilot to set transponder on position 'OFF'
To request pilot to switch from 'ON' to 'STBY'
Observation of compliance with an instruction to operate transponder from 'ON' to 'STBY' and back to 'ON'
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: Toggling the transponder between ON and STBY allows the controller to identify the corresponding target disappear and reappear on the radar screen.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: The Air Traffic Control Service: do not prevent collisions with terrain.
options: Wrong, they do prevent collisions with terrain
Except when an aircraft is flying IFR in IMC
Correct, except when an IFR flight is vectored by radar
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: ATC is not responsible for terrain clearance except when an IFR flight is being vectored by radar, where ATC provides minimum vectoring altitudes.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: Which code shall be used on mode 'A' to provide recognition of an emergency aircraft?
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: Transponder code 7700 is the international emergency code.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: One of the functions ensured by a radar control unit for the provision of approach control service is:
options: To apply a horizontal separation less than 5NM
To provide instructions in order to reduce separations minima, if accepted by the pilots
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: Approach control radar units are authorized to conduct Surveillance Radar Approaches (SRA) to guide aircraft onto final approach.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: The primary duty provided by a radar unit is:
options: To assist aircraft on the location of storms
To assist aircraft where navigation appears unsatisfactory
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: The primary objective of air traffic radar services is to provide safe separation between aircraft.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: What is meant when departure control instructs you to 'resume own navigation' after you have been vectored to an airway?
options: Advisories will no longer be issued by ATC
You are still in radar contact, but must make position reports
You should maintain that airway by use of your navigation equipment
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: This instruction advises the pilot to resume tracking the defined airway route using onboard navigation instruments.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.question: All aircraft carrying serviceable transponder shall operate the transponder:
options: At all times during flight, regardless of whether the aircraft is within or outside airspace where SSR is used for ATS purposes.
Only when the aircraft is flying within airspace where SSR is used for ATS purposes.
As and when required by the pilot
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.explanation: Regulations mandate that aircraft equipped with a functioning transponder must operate it continuously during flight unless instructed otherwise by ATC.
USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE.chapter: USE OF AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: Detailed description of meteorological information provided at the aerodrome and an indication of which meteorological office is responsible, is in the following part of the AIP:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: Aerodrome-specific meteorological details and responsible offices are found under the AD (Aerodromes) section of the AIP.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: A checklist of AIP supplements currently in force shall be issued at intervals of:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: Checklists of AIP supplements currently in force must be issued at intervals of not more than one month.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: Which of the following is information that is not given in AIP approach and landing charts?
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: Visibility minima are operational parameters determined by operators or regulatory authorities and are generally not specified directly on AIP approach charts.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: An integrated aeronautical information package consists of the following elements:
options: AIP, supplements to AIP; NOTAM and PIB, AIC and checklist summaries
AIP, including amendment service; supplements to AIP; NOTAM and pre-flight information bulletin (PIB), AIC, checklists and summaries
AIP including amendment service; supplements to AIP; NOTAM, AIC and checklist summaries
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: The Integrated Aeronautical Information Package comprises the AIP (with amendments), AIP Supplements, NOTAMs, PIB, AICs, and regular checklists/summaries.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: Temporary changes on specifications for AIP supplements of long duration and information of short duration which contains extensive text and/or graphics shall be published as AIP supplements. It is considered a long duration if it is:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: A period of three months or longer is treated as long duration for publishing AIP Supplements.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: Operationally significant changes to the AIP shall be published in accordance with:
options: AIC procedures and identified by the acronym AIC followed by a number
NOTAM procedures and identified by acronym NOTAM followed by a number
AIRAC procedures and identified by the acronym AIRAC
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: Operationally significant changes requiring advance notice are distributed following AIRAC procedures and identified by the acronym AIRAC.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: A checklist of NOTAM currently in force shall be issued via the AFTN at intervals of:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: A plain-language summary/checklist of valid NOTAMs must be promulgated via AFTN at intervals not exceeding one month.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: Change in frequency or location of navigational aids on short notice is notified through:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: Urgent operational changes such as nav-aid facility or frequency modifications on short notice are issued via NOTAM.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: The contents of Aeronautical Information Publication (AIP) are:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: Standard ICAO AIP formatting structures the publication into three core parts: GEN (General), ENR (En-route), and AD (Aerodromes).

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: The SIGMET service is described in the AIP in the following part:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: General meteorological services including SIGMET provisions are detailed within the GEN section (GEN 3.5) of the AIP.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: In which chapter of the AIP can you find a list with 'location indicators'?
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: Location indicators (ICAO four-letter codes) are published in Part 1 - General (GEN 2.4).

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: The information on holding, approach and departure procedures are found in the following part of the AIP:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: General holding, approach, and departure rules are cataloged under ENR (En-route) 1.5.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: The closure of a runway for a year, because of maintenance, will be published:
options: In NOTAM and AIP, inclusive Supplement
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: A long-term major change (such as a 1-year closure) is issued via NOTAM for immediate awareness and as an AIP Supplement for long-term tracking.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: An AIRAC is:
options: An acronym for a system aimed at advance notification based on common effective dates, of circumstances necessitating significant changes in operating procedures
A notice distributed by means of telecommunication containing information concerning the establishment, condition or change in any aeronautical facility service, procedure or hazard
A package which consists of the following elements: AIP supplements to the AIP, NOTAM, AIC, checklists and summaries
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: AIRAC (Aeronautical Information Regulation And Control) standardizes advance notification based on predefined, internationally agreed effective dates.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: Select the acronym corresponding to the following definition: a special NOTAM series notifying, by means of a specific format, an important change for aircraft operations due to volcanic activity, a volcanic eruption or a volcanic ash cloud.
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: ASHTAM is a dedicated NOTAM series warning of volcanic eruptions, ash clouds, or hazardous volcanic activity.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: The system notifying in advance the circumstances requiring important changes in the methods of operation, based on common effective dates, is identified by the acronym:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: AIRAC regulates advance notification based on coordinated, standardized effective calendar dates.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: The temporary, long-term modification (3 months or more) and the short-term extensive or graphical information are published as follows:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: Temporary changes lasting 3 months or longer, or those with complex graphics/text, are published as AIP Supplements.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: The information concerning charges for aerodromes/heliports and Air Navigation Services are on the following part of the AIP:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: Tariffs and service fees for aerodromes and navigation infrastructure are published in GEN 4.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: A notice providing information on Rules of the Air, Traffic Services and Navigation Procedures and distributed in advance of its effective date is:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: Significant procedural operational changes promulgated in advance are distributed via the AIRAC system.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: A notice containing information concerning flight safety, air navigation, technical, administrative or legislative matters and originated at the AIS of a state is called:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: AICs are notices containing administrative, technical, safety, or legislative guidance that do not qualify for a NOTAM or AIP inclusion.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: In which section of AIP are contained information elements relating to prohibited, restricted and dangerous areas?
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: Special airspace designations like Prohibited, Restricted, and Danger areas are cataloged in ENR 5.1.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: In which section of AIP are contained information elements to refueling facilities and limitations on refueling services?
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: Ground handling services, including fueling availability and limits, are listed under the AD section for each aerodrome.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: In which section of the AIP are contained information elements relating to areas and/or routes for which meteorological service is provided?
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: General meteorology responsibilities, coverage zones, and routes are detailed in GEN 3.5.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: Each contracting state shall provide an Aeronautical Information Service (AIS) in its territory and for areas in which the state is responsible for the Air Traffic Services outside its territory, and this shall include the preparation and origination of:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: ICAO Annex 15 mandates states to prepare and originate a complete Integrated Aeronautical Information Package.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: The identification of each prohibited, restricted and danger area shall be composed by:
options: The nationality letters for location indicators assigned to the state or territory, followed by the letters P, R and D and figures
The letters P (Prohibited), R (Restricted) and D (Dangerous) for the area concerned and figures
The letters P (Prohibited), R (Restricted) and D (Dangerous) followed by figures
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: Special airspace identifiers use nationality letters followed by P/R/D and a unique identification number (e.g., VOD25).

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: NOF in India are established at:
options: International Airports at Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai only.
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: International NOTAM Offices (NOF) in India are located at the four major international hubs: Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Chennai.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: Runway Condition Report (RCR) is prepared by ____ for use by ____:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: The Aerodrome Operator generates the Runway Condition Report (RCR) to provide flight crews with assessed runway surface information.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: Runway Condition Code (RWYCC) is reported for:
options: The runway to indicate unusable portion of the operational runway.
Each one third portion of the operational runway to indicate the presence of water, snow, ice, slush or frost.
For non operational runway to denote its status.
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: RWYCC values are reported for each third of the runway length to accurately reflect contamination levels.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: Standing water on runway is notified through a:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: SNOWTAM formats are utilized for surface condition assessments including standing water, slush, ice, or snow.

AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.question: NOF stands for:
AERONAUTICAL INFORMATION SERVICES.explanation: NOF is the standard ICAO acronym for International NOTAM Office.

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: The units responsible for promoting efficient organization of search and rescue service are:
options: Area control centre, flight information centre and rescue coordination centre
Rescue coordination centre and rescue sub-centres
Alerting centre and rescue coordination centre
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: Rescue Coordination Centres (RCC) and Rescue Sub-Centres (RSC) are the primary operational units responsible for the efficient organization and execution of SAR services within a search and rescue region.

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question:
Three aircraft, (1), (2) and (3) arrive successively at ten minute intervals, overhead the scene of a recent aircraft accident.
- aircraft (1) is unable to establish contact with the Search and Rescue Centre
- aircraft (2) is able to contact the Search and Rescue Centre
- aircraft (3) is a Search and Rescue helicopter
The command of the situation is the responsibility of:
options: (1), then by mutual consent (2) and then (3)
(1), and then by mutual consent to (3)
(1), then by mutual consent (2) until the completion of operations
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: The first aircraft on scene assumes command until communication is established and control is passed to a better-equipped aircraft (2), and subsequently handed over to dedicated SAR assets (3).

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: What is the meaning of the symbol 'V' in the ground-air visual signal code for use by survivors?
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: In ground-air visual signal codes used by survivors, 'V' stands for 'Require assistance'.

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: What is the meaning of the symbol 'LLL' in the ground-air visual signal code for use by rescue units?
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: In ground-air visual signals used by rescue units, 'LLL' indicates 'Operation completed'.

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: Which of the following is NOT an international distress frequency?
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: Standard international distress frequencies include 121.5 MHz (VHF), 243.0 MHz (UHF military), and 2182 kHz (MF maritime), making 2430 kHz incorrect.

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: An aircraft is flying over a mountainous region in which a search is being carried out to find the survivors of an aircraft accident. The pilot sees a ground signal in the form of an 'X'. This indicates:
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: In survivor ground-air visual signals, the symbol 'X' signifies 'Require medical assistance'.

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: At night an aircraft observes a luminous signal requesting help. To indicate that he has received these ground signals, the pilot must:
options: Make at least one complete turn over the group of people in difficulty
Transmit, by luminous Morse signal, a series of the letter 'R' using his navigational lights
Switch his landing lights on and off twice or, if he is not so equipped, his navigation lights twice
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: An aircraft acknowledges visual ground signals at night by flashing landing lights or navigation lights twice.

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: The color identification of the contents of droppable containers and packages containing survival equipment should take the form of coloured streamers according to the following code:
options: Red for medical supplies and first aid equipment
Blue for blankets and protective clothing
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: According to ICAO Annex 12, red streamers denote containers carrying medical supplies and first aid equipment.

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: COSPAS-SARSAT is:
options: A communication system linking all aircraft
A space system for the search of vessels in distress
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: COSPAS-SARSAT is an international satellite-based search and rescue system designed to detect and locate emergency beacons (ELTs/EPIRBs).

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: You are flying in Mumbai FIR when you intercept a distress call. You record the message and tell Mumbai FIC. The radio operator at Mumbai tells you to standby. What should you consider doing whilst awaiting instructions?
options: Make a general call on 121.5 asking other airplanes to assist
Descend to low level and carry out a surface search for ships
Proceed to the position given in the distress message
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: While awaiting instructions from the responsible ATS/SAR unit, pilots intercepting a distress message should evaluate heading toward the transmitted distress coordinates.

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: Search and Rescue services within the territory of ICAO contracting states are provided:
options: When the authority of the contracting state decides to do so
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: ICAO Contracting States are obligated to maintain Search and Rescue services operational on a continuous 24-hour basis.

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: Contracting States shall establish a rescue co-ordination centre:
options: In each search and rescue region.
If they are adjacent to the sea.
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: States must establish a Rescue Coordination Centre (RCC) for each designated Search and Rescue Region (SRR).

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: A Rescue Unit is:
options: A unit assisting a RCC in SAR duties.
A unit composed of trained personnel and provided with equipment suitable for the expeditious conduct of SAR.
A unit responsible for SAR service in co-operation with a RCC.
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: A Rescue Unit is defined as a unit composed of trained personnel and provided with equipment suitable for the prompt and efficient conduct of search and rescue operations.

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: Which of the following statements regarding Alerting service is correct?
options: Aircraft in the vicinity of an aircraft known or believed to be the subject of unlawful interference, shall be informed about this;
The Alert phase is established when no communication has been received from an aircraft within a period of thirty minutes after the time a communication should have been received;
Alerting Service and Flight Information Service are often provided by the same ATS unit
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: Alerting Service is inherently co-located with Flight Information Service and provided by the same ATS units (e.g., FIC or Area Control Center).

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: Whenever a distress signal and/or message or equivalent transmission is intercepted by the PIC of an aircraft, he shall:
options: Record the position of the craft in distress if given and if possible take a bearing on the transmission
If possible take a bearing on the transmission
Record the position of the craft in distress if given
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: Upon intercepting a distress call, the PIC must log the transmitted coordinates and take a radio bearing on the signal if equipment permits.

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: What is the meaning of SAR signal 'N' when used by survivors on the ground:
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: In ground-air visual sign code for survivors, the letter 'N' indicates 'No' or 'Negative'.

SEARCH AND RESCUE.question: Survival equipment, dropped by SAR and containing food and water will be packed in containers and indicated by streamers of following colour:
SEARCH AND RESCUE.explanation: Under standard international SAR color-coding, blue streamers indicate containers carrying food and water.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Which of the following Annexes to the Chicago convention contains minimum specifications for the design of aerodromes?
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Annex 14 to the Convention on International Civil Aviation contains the Standards and Recommended Practices (SARPs) for aerodrome design and operations.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: "Clearway" is a defined rectangular area established to:
options: Reduce the risk of damage to aircraft running off a runway
Protect aircraft during take-off or landing operations
Permit aircraft to make a portion of its initial climb to a specific height
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: A clearway is an area beyond the runway under the control of airport authorities over which an aircraft may perform a portion of its initial climb to a specified height.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: The STOPWAY is a defined rectangular area on the ground at the end of take-off run available prepared as a suitable area where:
options: A landing aircraft can be stopped if overcoming the end of runway
An aircraft can be stopped in the case of an abandoned take-off
A landing aircraft can be stopped only in emergency
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: A stopway is prepared at the end of the take-off run available to safely decelerate and bring an aircraft to a stop in the event of an aborted takeoff.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: "ASDA" (Accelerate Stop Distance Available) is:
options: The length of the take-off run available plus the length of stopway and clearway (if provided)
The length of the take-off run available plus the length of stopway (if stopway provided)
The length of the runway plus the length of stopway available (if stopway provided)
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: ASDA is defined as the length of the take-off run available (TORA) plus the length of any stopway provided.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: "Instrument runways" are the following runways intended for the operation of aircraft using instrument approach procedures:
options: Non precision approach runways, precision approach runways category I, II and III
Instrument approach runways, precision approach runways category I, II and III
Precision approach runways category I, II and III
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Instrument runways include non-precision approach runways and precision approach runways (Category I, II, and III).

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: "TODA" take-off distance available is:
options: The length of the take-off run available plus the length of the clearway (if provided)
The length of the take-off run available plus the length of stopway and clearway (if provided)
The length of the take-off run plus the length of the stopway
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: TODA is defined as the length of the take-off run available (TORA) plus the length of the clearway, if provided.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: The light shown by an "Aerodrome Identification Beacon" at a land aerodrome shall be:
options: White and green colour identification given by Morse Code
Green colour identification given by Morse Code
Blue colour identification given by Morse Code
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: At land aerodromes, an aerodrome identification beacon shows green flashes identifying the aerodrome in Morse Code.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Taxiway edge lights shall be:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Standard taxiway edge lights are fixed lights emitting blue color.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: In the case of parallel runways, each runway designation number shall be supplemented:
options: By a letter - for example 2 parallel runways "L" and "R" and for 3 "L", "C" and "R"
By a letter for 2 parallel runways
By a number like "0" and "01" for 2 parallel runways
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Parallel runways are differentiated by letters: 'L' and 'R' for two parallel runways, and 'L', 'C', and 'R' for three parallel runways.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: In the "PAPI" system the pilot during an approach will see the two units nearest the runway as red and the two units farthest from the runway as white when:
options: On or close to the approach slope
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: When an aircraft is on or close to the approach glide path, a PAPI displays two white lights on the outer units and two red lights on the inner units.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Runway threshold identification lights, when provided, should be:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Runway Threshold Identification Lights (RTILs) are flashing white lights located on each side of the threshold.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: What is a "barrette"?
options: Three or more ground lights closely spaced together to appear as a bar of lights
A frangible structure on which approach lights are fixed
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: A barrette is three or more ground lights closely spaced transverse to the approach/runway centerline to appear as a continuous bar of light.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: What is the length of an approach lighting system of a precision-approach runway CAT II:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Precision approach lighting systems for CAT II and III runways extend to a length of 900 meters.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Runway end lights shall be:
options: Fixed unidirectional lights showing red in the direction of the runway
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Runway end lights are fixed unidirectional lights emitting red in the direction of the runway towards an aircraft taking off or landing.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Aerodrome signs should be in the following configuration:
options: mandatory instruction signs, black backgrounds with red inscriptions
information signs, yellow or black background with black or yellow inscriptions
mandatory instruction signs, red background with black inscriptions
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Information signs consist of yellow or black backgrounds with contrasting black or yellow inscriptions.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: The "PAPI" shall consist of:
options: Two wing bars of 4 sharp transition multi-lamp or paired units equally spaced
A wing bar of 4 sharp transition multi-lamp or paired units equally spaced
Two wing bars of 6 sharp transition multi-lamp or paired units equally spaced
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: A standard PAPI installation consists of a single wing bar of 4 sharp transition light units placed perpendicular to the runway.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Runway threshold lights shall be:
options: Fixed lights showing green or white colours
Fixed unidirectional lights showing green in the direction of approach to the runway
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Threshold lights are fixed unidirectional lights displaying green in the direction of approach to the runway.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Taxiway centerline lights other than an exit taxiway shall be:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Standard taxiway centerline lights emit fixed green light along taxiways.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: How many red lights must a pilot see, whose aircraft, in final approach, is following a normal glide path defined by a PAPI?
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: On a normal glide path, a pilot observing a 4-unit PAPI will see two red lights (and two white lights).

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Runway edge lights expected in the case of a displaced threshold shall be:
options: Fixed lights, white or yellow colour
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Runway edge lights along the displaced threshold area show variable white towards the landing direction.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: The abbreviation PAPI stands for:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: PAPI stands for Precision Approach Path Indicator.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: High intensity obstacle lights should be:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: High-intensity obstacle lights are flashing white lights used on structures exceeding certain heights.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Low intensity obstacle lights on mobile objects shall be:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Low-intensity obstacle lights on mobile vehicles (excluding emergency vehicles) are flashing yellow or blue.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Low intensity obstacle lights on fixed objects shall be:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Low-intensity obstacle lights on fixed structures are fixed red or flashing red lights.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: The runway edge lights shall be:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Runway edge lights are predominantly white, except for the caution zone on the last 600m or one-third of the runway.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: The aerodrome category for rescue and fire fighting is based on:
options: The over-all length of the longest aeroplane normally using the aerodrome and its maximum fuselage width
The over-all length of the longest aeroplane
The longest aeroplane maximum width only
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: RFFS categories are calculated based on overall airplane length and maximum fuselage width of the longest aircraft using the airport.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Regarding declared airfield distances the ASDA is:
options: The distance from the start of the take-off run to the last point capable of bearing the full weight of the aircraft under normal operating conditions
The distance from the start of the take-off run to the end of the stopway
The area beyond the end of the prepared surface only available to stopping in an emergency
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Accelerate-Stop Distance Available (ASDA) represents TORA plus the length of any available stopway.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: "A defined rectangular area on the ground at the end of take-off run available prepared as a suitable area in which an aircraft can be stopped in the case of an abandoned take-off" is the definition for:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: This is the official ICAO definition of a Stopway.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Where a parking bay is provided at an aerodrome suitable for the parking of an aircraft which is known or believed to be the subject of unlawful interference, what is the minimum distance that this parking bay needs to be separated from any other parking areas, buildings...
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Isolated aircraft parking positions dedicated to hijacked aircraft must be located at least 100 meters away from other parking stands or structures.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Crash/Rescue (emergency) services provision is categorised according to physical characteristics of the type of aeroplane using the aerodrome. Upon what are the categories based?
options: Overall length and maximum takeoff mass
Maximum number of passengers on board
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Aerodrome fire fighting categories depend on the overall length of aircraft and maximum fuselage width.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: How is a paved pre-threshold area which is greater than 60 m in length but not suitable for any use by aircraft, marked?
options: By white arrows directing approaching aircraft to the displaced threshold
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Permanently unusable paved areas preceding a threshold greater than 60m are marked with large yellow chevrons pointing toward the threshold.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Which of the following systems describes an abbreviated precision approach path indicator (A-PAPI):
options: Ten light units arranged on one side of the runway in the form of a single wing bar of four light units, with a bisecting longitudinal line of six lights
Twenty light units symmetrically disposed about the runway centre line in the form of two wing bars of four light units each, with bisecting longitudinal lines of six lights
A wing bar of 2 sharp transition multi-lamp units normally located on the left side of the runway unless it is physically impracticable to do so
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: An Abbreviated PAPI (A-PAPI) consists of a wing bar of 2 light units located typically on the left side of the runway.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: What colour are emergency vehicles painted that are used on the manoeuvring area of an aerodrome?
options: A single conspicuous colour, preferably red or yellowish green
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Emergency vehicles must be painted in a single highly visible color, preferably red or yellowish-green.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Alternate yellow/green centre line lights of a taxiway indicate:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Alternating green and yellow taxiway centerline lights indicate that the taxiway is within an ILS/MLS critical or sensitive area.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: When taxiing on a surface with white markings, you are rolling on a:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: White surface markings are used exclusively for runways; taxiways and aprons use yellow markings.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: What colour are apron safety line markings?
options: A contrasting colour from the taxiway markings
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Apron safety lines must be painted in a conspicuous color contrasting with taxiway markings (often white).

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Runway centre line lights shall be fixed lights showing variable... from the threshold to the point 900m from the runway end, alternate... and variable... from 900m to 300m from runway end, and... from 300m to the runway end.
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Runway centerline lights display white until the last 900m, alternate red and white from 900m to 300m, and red for the final 300m.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: What colour is an aerodrome beacon at a land aerodrome?
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Land aerodrome beacons show green flashes, or alternating white and green flashes.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Which of the following describes a location sign?
options: Red writing on a white background
Yellow writing on a black background
Black writing on a yellow background
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: A taxiway/runway location sign consists of yellow inscriptions/text on a black background surrounded by a yellow border.
