VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: When on or close to the approach slope, the wing bar of a PAPI shows:
options: Two red lights and two white lights
Three white lights and one red light
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: When accurately following the defined glide path, a PAPI displays two red lights and two white lights.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Which of the following is not a mandatory instruction sign:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Direction signs are information signs (black lettering on yellow background), not mandatory instruction signs.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: The number of stripes on each side of the centre line of a runway threshold marking which has a width of 45m is:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: For a 45m wide runway, a total of 12 threshold stripes are required (6 stripes on each side of the centerline).

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Mandatory instructions signs on an aerodrome shall have the following colours:
options: White inscription on a red background
Yellow inscription on a black background
Black inscription on a yellow background
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Mandatory instruction signs feature white text/inscriptions on a red background.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Taxiway markings and aircraft stand markings are:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Surface markings on taxiways and aircraft parking stands are painted yellow.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Taxiway centre line lights other than an exit taxiway shall be:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Taxiway centerline lights show fixed green lights.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: ARIWS is a system used for:
options: warning a pilot about bird activity on take off path
cautioning a pilot about wind shear on finals in real time
warning a pilot about runway incursion in near real time
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Autonomous Runway Incursion Warning Systems (ARIWS) automatically detect potential runway incursions and alert flight crews in real time.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: You see a board painted in white with letters in red on taxytrack edge. This board is a:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Signs displaying red backgrounds/letters indicate mandatory instructions requiring ATC clearance to proceed.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: An aiming point marking shall be provided at:
options: each approach end of paved instrument runway
paved taxy track joining precision approach runway
paved runways not provided with touch down zone markings
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Aiming point markings are mandatory at each approach end of a paved instrument runway.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: LFFZ is established around an aerodrome to:
options: protect aircraft from low flying aircraft
protect aircraft from low flying fighter aircraft in military areas
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Laser-Free Flight Zones (LFFZ) protect flight operations in critical phases around aerodromes from hazardous laser beam emissions.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: VASIS shall be provided to serve the approach to a runway:
options: not served by visual approach aids
not served by non visual approach aids
whether or not the runway is served by visual approach aids or by non-visual aids, where turbo jet operations take place
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Visual approach slope indicator systems are required for jet operations regardless of other non-visual or visual approach aids.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Identify the correct Taxiway designator:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Taxiways are designated using letters of the alphabet (e.g., Taxiway C or Charlie), whereas runways use magnetic headings.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Wildlife hazard at aerodromes is caused due to the presence of:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Wildlife hazards encompass risks presented by both birds and ground animals on or around aerodromes.

VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.question: Aerodrome Operations Vehicles are considered to be:
VISUAL AIDS FOR NAVIGATION.explanation: Vehicles operating on the movement area can deposit debris, making them a potential source of Foreign Object Debris (FOD).

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: PANS-OPS means:
options: Procedures for Air Navigation Services - Aircraft operations
Pilots Alternate Navigational Systems and Operational Procedures
Procedures for Air Navigation Systems - Airfield operations
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: PANS-OPS stands for Procedures for Air Navigation Services – Aircraft Operations.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: The document that specifies the recommendations for instrument procedures is called...
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: ICAO Doc 8168 contains the PANS-OPS provisions for visual and instrument flight procedures.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Which of the following defines transition altitude?
options: The altitude above which the vertical position of an aircraft is determined by reference to local QHN
The altitude below which the vertical position of an aircraft is determined by reference to QNH
The altitude at which 1013 hPa is set and vertical position then reported as a flight level
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Transition altitude is the altitude at or below which the vertical position of an aircraft is controlled by reference to altitudes (QNH).
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: The Transition Level:
options: Is published for the aerodrome in the Section ENR of the AIP
Shall be the lowest flight level available for use above the transition altitude
Is calculated and declared for an approach by the Pilot-in command
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: The transition level is the lowest flight level available for use above the transition altitude.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: During flight through the transition layer the vertical position of the aircraft should be expressed as
options: Altitude above mean sea level during climb.
Either altitude above mean sea level or flight level during climb
Altitude above mean sea level during descent
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: During climb through the transition layer, vertical position is expressed as flight level, while during descent it is expressed as altitude.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Transition from altitude to flight level, and vice-versa is done:
options: At transition level during climb and transition altitude during descent
At transition altitude during climb and transition level during descent
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Altimeter setting is changed from QNH to standard (1013.25 hPa) when climbing through transition altitude, and to QNH when descending through transition level.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Which of the following cruising levels would you select under the following conditions: True track 358°, variation 3°E, deviation 2°W?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Magnetic track = True track (358°) - Variation (3°E) = 355°. According to the semi-circular rule, westbound tracks (180°-359°) use even flight levels or VFR odd-plus-500 levels as applicable.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: In the vicinity of an aerodrome that is going to be used by the aircraft the vertical position of the aircraft shall be expressed in:
options: Altitude above sea level on or above the transition altitude
Flight level on or below the transition level
Altitude above sea level on or below the transition altitude
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Vertical position at or below the transition altitude is expressed in terms of altitude (QNH).
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: The vertical position of an aircraft at or below the transition altitude will be reported:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Positions at or below transition altitude are reported as altitude above mean sea level.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: The transition altitude of an aerodrome should not be below:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Transition altitude shall normally be specified by the State and should not be lower than 3,000 ft (or 4,000 ft in some regulatory contexts).
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: The pilot of a departing aircraft flying under IFR shall change the altimeter setting from QNH to standard setting 1013.25hPA when passing:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: When climbing, the switch to standard pressure setting (1013.25 hPa) is made at the transition altitude.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: In the standard atmosphere FL150 is equivalent to:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: FL150 corresponds to 15,000 feet, which is approximately 4,572 metres (closest choice 4,550 m).
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: A pre-flight altimeter check should be carried out:
options: At a known elevation on the aerodrome
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Pre-flight altimeter accuracy checks are performed at a point of known elevation on the aerodrome.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Which of the following correctly lists special purpose codes that are to be used in conjunction with Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR)?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Standard emergency SSR codes are: 7700 for general emergency/distress, 7500 for unlawful interference/hijack, and 7600 for radio failure.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: When acknowledging mode/code setting instructions, pilots shall:
options: Read back the mode and code to be set
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: ATC transponder mode and code assignments must always be read back by the pilot.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Pilots shall not operate the SSR special position indicator (IDENT) feature unless:
options: They operate a transponder with Mode C
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: The IDENT feature should only be activated when specifically instructed by air traffic control.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: When the aircraft carries serviceable Mode C equipment, the pilot:
options: Shall continuously operate this mode only when the aircraft is within controlled arspace
Shall continuously operate this mode regardless of ATC instructions
Shall continuously operate this mode unless otherwise directed by ATC
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Mode C pressure-altitude reporting must be operated continuously unless ATC explicitly directs otherwise.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: When an aircraft carries a serviceable transponder, the pilot shall operate the transponder:
options: At all times during flight, regardless of whether the aircraft is within or outside airspace where SSR is used for ATS purposes
Only when the aircraft is flying within controlled airspace
Only when the aircraft is flying within airspace where SSR is used for ATS purposes
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Pilots must operate transponders at all times during flight unless otherwise directed by ATC.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Your transponder code assigned by ATC is 5320. In flight, in case of radio communications failure, you will squawk code:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: In the event of a radio communication failure, code 7600 must be set on Mode A.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: The pilot of an aircraft losing two-way communication shall set the transponder to Mode A Code:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Code 7600 is reserved globally for loss of radio communication.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: When the aircraft carries serviceable Mode C transponder, the pilot shall continuously operate this mode:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Mode C altitude encoding should run continuously unless ATC orders otherwise.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: During a pre-flight a SSR transponder is found to be inoperative and immediate repair is not possible:
options: A flight to the closest airport, where a repair can be made is allowed
A flight can not be made
It is necessary to specify this failure in the appropriate field of the flight plan
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Flight to the nearest station where repairs can be effected is generally permitted subject to ATC clearance.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: When an aircraft is subjected to unlawful interference, the pilot-in-command shall indicate the situation by setting the transponder to:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Code 7500 indicates unlawful interference (hijack).
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: On receipt of a TA, pilots shall:
options: Respond immediately by following the TA as indicated
Not manoeuvre their aircraft in response to traffc advisories (TAS) only
Notify the appropriate ATC unit of the TA
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Pilots must not initiate evasive maneuvers based solely on Traffic Advisories (TA); maneuvers are only permitted in response to Resolution Advisories (RA).
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Airborne collision avoidance system (ACAS) indications shall be used by pilots in:
options: Both B) and C) are correct.
The active search for, and visual acquisition of, conflicting traffic.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: ACAS indications assist both in enhancing situational awareness and helping visually acquire conflicting traffic.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What are the two main objective of altimeter setting?
options: To read height and barometric pressure
QNH to be set in the vicinity of the aerodrome and QFE en route
To provide adequate terrain clearance and vertical separation
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Altimeter settings ensure adequate clearance above obstacles/terrain and vertical separation between aircraft.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Which of the following correctly defines altitude?
options: Vertical position with reference to MSL
Vertical position with reference to aerodrome elevation
Vertical position with reference to touchdown
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Altitude is the vertical distance of a level, point, or object measured from Mean Sea Level (MSL).
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Which of the following correctly defines height?
options: Vertical position with reference to MSL
Vertical position with reference to aerodrome elevation
Vertical position with reference to touchdown
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Height is the vertical distance of a level, point, or object measured from a specified datum (such as aerodrome elevation).
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Which of the following correctly defines flight level?
options: Vertical position with reference to MSL
Vertical position with reference to aerodrome elevation
Vertical position with reference to the standard pressure level
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: A Flight Level is a surface of constant atmospheric pressure related to a specific pressure datum of 1013.2 hPa.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: If the QNH is 991 Mb where is FL?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: When QNH is below standard pressure (1013.25 - 991 = 22.25 hPa), the 1013.25 hPa datum datum surface lies below MSL.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Which of the following is the location of FL?
options: The first flight level above the transition level
The level defined with reference to a QNH of 1013.25mb
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Flight Levels are referenced to the standard atmospheric pressure datum of 1013.25 hPa (mb).
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What is the relationship between IFR and VFR flight level?
options: For given mag track, the VFR level is the IFR level plus 500' if below FL290
IFR levels are flown on mag tracks from 000 to 179 an VFR levels from 180 to 359
VFR levels may be flown in VMC or IMC, but IFR levels must only be flown in IMC
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: VFR cruising levels below FL290 are 500 ft above the corresponding IFR level for a given magnetic track.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: At what point in a flight is the QNH communicated to the pilot by ATC?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: The QNH altimeter setting is routinely provided to departing aircraft in the taxi clearance.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: If you are flying outside an aerodrome traffic zone, what are you required to set On your altimeter sub scale ?
options: The lowest forecast pressure setting with respect to MSL for the area in which you are flying
The local QNH obtained from FIS or the nearest aerodrome
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Outside controlled/aerodrome airspace below transition altitude, aircraft set the local QNH from FIS or the nearest station.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: If you are flying en route below the transition level but are well briefed with regard to safety altitude, from where would you get altimeter setting information whilst airborne?
options: You only need the departure aerodrome and destination aerodrome QNH and then interpolate the difference whilst en route
Ask the met man to forecast the QNH for the route before you take off
Ask the FIS controller for local aerodrome QNHs
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: En-route QNH updates are obtained airborne from the Flight Information Service (FIS) controller.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: You are approaching an aerodrome to land and call the approach controller at 10nm from the edge of the ATZ. Your flight conditions are VMC and you are flying VFR. When would you expect to be advised to set the aerodrome QNH?
options: On initial contact the app controller will pass QNH and tell you what altitude to fly at
On clearance to enter the traffic pattern established for a visual join to land
When descending below the transition altitude
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: When approaching for a visual join, the aerodrome QNH is provided with the clearance to enter the traffic pattern.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: You test your altimeter with aerodrome QNH set. What would a serviceable altimeter read?
options: The height of the aeroplane above the datum
The elevation of the position of the aeroplane plus the height of the altimeter static vent
The altitude of the aeroplane above the datum
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: With QNH set on the ground, the altimeter reads airfield elevation plus static port height above ground.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question:
In selecting a flight level for a flight, which of the following should be taken into consideration ?
1. Adequate terrain clearance is ensured
2. ATC requirements (Danger Areas, restricted airspace etc.) are complied with
3. Minimum traffic separation is ensured
4. Adequate separation from VFR traffic is ensured (differential flight levels applied)
5. The level chosen complies with the table of cruising levels
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Selecting an en-route cruising flight level requires terrain clearance, airspace compliance, and adherence to the table of cruising levels.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What is the minimum gradient for missed approach procedure?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: The standard design climb gradient for a missed approach procedure is 2.5%.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: You are entering a FIR where SSR is used from an area where SSR is not used. What would you squawk?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: When entering SSR airspace without an assigned code, squawk Mode A 2000 with Mode C unless instructed otherwise.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Your aircraft is subjected to unlawful interference (hi jacking). Without upsetting the man with the gun, what would you squawk?
options: Either M 700 or A.17500 depending upon the situation
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Code 7500 on Mode A indicates unlawful interference.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What are you required to do if you become aware that your transponder has failed?
options: Try recycling the transponder and set 7777 to maximise the response
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: In the event of a transponder failure in flight, the pilot must inform ATC immediately.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Which of the following is an invalid squawk?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Transponder codes are octal numbers using digits 0–7 only; digits 8 and 9 are invalid.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: On a single SSR control box/selector system (ie no changeover switch), what is the correct procedure for changing squawk?
options: Squawk 'standby', then change the code; then squawk 'normal'.
Squawk 'off', then change the code; then Squawk 'normal'.
Only change one digit at a time
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Switching to Standby before changing codes prevents transiently sending emergency codes (like 7500/7600/7700) across the dials.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What does the abbreviation ACAS mean?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: ACAS stands for Airborne Collision Avoidance System.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What does the abbreviation OIS mean?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: OIS stands for Obstacle Identification Surface.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What does the abbreviation DER mean?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: DER stands for Departure End of Runway.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: The MSA, which must be established around a navigation facility, is in general valid within a sector of:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Minimum Sector Altitude (MSA) provides 300 m (1000 ft) obstacle clearance within a 25 NM radius of a navigation facility.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What is defined as the portion of a flight in which the aircraft descends below 1000 ft above the relevant DH or MDH?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: The final phase leading to visual landing below 1,000 ft relative to DH/MDH is the approach to landing phase.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: A radial is:
options: A magnetic bearing to or from a VOR station, depending on whether the aircraft is inbound or outbound to or from the VOR
A magnetic bearing to a VOR station
A magnetic bearing extending from a VOR station
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: A radial is defined as a magnetic bearing extending outward from a VOR station.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: A circling approach is:
options: A flight manoeuvre to be performed only under radar vectoring
A visual flight manoeuvre keeping the runway in sight
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: A circling approach is a visual flight maneuver performed after an instrument approach to align with a runway not suited for a straight-in approach, keeping the runway in sight.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What is the meaning of MEHT?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: MEHT stands for Minimum Eye Height over Threshold.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: OCH for a precision approach is defined as:
options: The lowest height above mean sea level of the relevant runway used establishing compliance with appropriate obstacle clearance requirements
The lowest altitude above the aerodrome elevation used in establishing compliance with appropriate obstacle clearance requirements
The lowest height above the elevation of the relevant runway threshold, at which a missed approach must be initiated to ensure compliance with the appropriate obstacle clearance criteria
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Obstacle Clearance Height (OCH) for precision approaches is referenced to the threshold elevation.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: The approach categories of aircraft are based upon:
options: 1.3 times the stalling speed in clean configuration at minimum certified landing mass
1.3 times the stalling speed in the landing configuration at minimum certified landing mass
1.3 times the stalling speed in the landing configuration at maximum certified landing mass
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Aircraft approach categories are determined by 1.3 times the stall speed (Vat) in the landing configuration at maximum certified landing mass.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Maximum permissible bank angle in a holding pattern is _____ degrees:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Holding pattern turns should be made at a rate of 3°/sec or a bank angle of 25°, whichever requires the lesser bank.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: The term used to describe the visual phase of flight after completing an instrument approach, to bring an aircraft into position for landing on runway which is not suitably located for straight-in approach, is:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Visual maneuvering (circling) is used when a straight-in landing is not possible following an instrument approach.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: In a straight departure, the initial departure track is of the alignment of the runway centreline within:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: A straight departure is one where the departure track is within 15° of the alignment of the runway centerline.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: In an instrument departure procedure the minimum obstacle clearance at the departure end of runway equals:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Screen height/obstacle clearance directly at the departure end of the runway (DER) is specified as 0 ft in basic design criteria.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: We can distinguish two types of departure routes. During a straight departure the initial departure track is within:
options: 15° of the alignment of the runway centreline
10° of the alignment of the runway centreline
25° of the alignment of the runway centreline
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Initial departure track within 15° of runway centerline alignment constitutes a straight departure.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: If in an instrument departure procedure the track to be followed by the aeroplane is published, the pilot is expected:
options: To correct for known wind to remain within the protected airspace
To request from ATC different heading for wind correction
To ignore the wind and proceed on a heading equal to the track
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Pilots must apply appropriate wind correction to track the published track centerline and remain within protected airspace.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: In general, which is the main factor that dictates the design of an instrument departure procedure?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Surrounding terrain is the primary factor determining instrument departure procedure design and gradients.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: During an omni-directional departure, what height are you required to climb to before turning onto the desired track?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Turns during an omni-directional departure must not be initiated until reaching 120 m (394 ft) above the DER elevation.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: The main factor that dictates in general the design of an instrument departure procedure is:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Terrain around the aerodrome is the dominant factor influencing departure procedure layout.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: SID terminates at:
options: the first fix of the en-route phase.
point 15 nms from DER on departure leg.
fix decided by the pilot before reaching TOC
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Standard Instrument Departures (SIDs) terminate at a designated fix on the en-route structure.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: A public transport aircraft shall not take-off unless the following minima departure airfield are satisfactory:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Takeoff minima specify required ceiling (cloud ceiling) and runway visual range (RVR).
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Obstacle clearance for an ILS approach is based on the assumption that the pilot does not deviate from the centreline more than:
options: half scale deflection of the localizer indicator
full scale deflection of the localizer indicator
half scale deflection of the glidepath indicator and horizontal 35° off the centreline
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: ILS obstacle clearance criteria assume aircraft remain within half-scale deflection of localizer center guidance.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Who establishes the OCA/H (Obstacle Clearance Altitude/Height) for an approach procedure?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: The State authority designs the approach procedure and establishes the OCA/H.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: If visual reference is lost while circling to land from an instrument approach, it is expected that the pilot will make an initial climbing turn towards the:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: When visual reference is lost during circling, the pilot must make an initial climbing turn toward the landing runway before joining the missed approach track.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: A circling approach is:
options: A visual flight manoeuvre keeping the runway in sight
A visual flight manoeuvre to be conducted only in IMC
A flight manoeuvre to be performed only under radar vectoring
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Circling is a visual maneuver flown after an instrument approach while continuously keeping the runway environment in sight.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: When the visual manoeuvring (circling) area has been established the obstacle clearance altitude/height (OCA/H) is determined:
options: Only for categories C, D and E aircraft
For each category of aircraft, and it may be different for each one of them
For all categories of aircraft, and it is the same for all of them
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Circling OCA/H is determined separately for each aircraft category based on speed and turning radius differences.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: On a non-precision approach a so-called "straight-in-approach" is considered acceptable, if the angle between the final approach track and the runway centreline is:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: A non-precision approach allows straight-in minima if the final approach track intersects the runway centerline extension at 30° or less.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: If contact is lost with the runway on the downwind leg of a circling manoeuvre, what actions should be taken?
options: Turn towards the inner marker for the runway in use, maintaining circling altitude
If you have other visual cues, continue with ground contact
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: If visual contact with the landing runway is lost at any point during circling, a missed approach must be initiated immediately.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Minimum sector altitudes are determined by the inbound radial in relation to the IAF. These sectors are established for a distance from the IAF of:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Minimum Sector Altitudes (MSA) cover a standard 25 NM radius centered on the navigation facility/IAF.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: A "precision approach" is a direct instrument approach...
options: using bearing, elevation and distance information
carried out by a crew of at least two pilots trained with a specific working method
using at least one source of bearing information and one source of elevation or distance information
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Precision approaches provide both lateral (bearing) and vertical (elevation/glidepath) guidance alongside distance information.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: The term used to describe the visual phase of flight after completing an instrument approach, to bring an aircraft into position for landing on runway which is not suitably located for straight-in approach is:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Visual maneuvering (circling) is used to align with a runway when straight-in approach requirements are not met.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: In a precision approach (ILS), the final approach segment begins at the:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: For precision approaches (ILS), the final approach segment begins at the Final Approach Point (FAP) where glide path interception occurs.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Under which conditions may an aircraft on a straight-in-VOR approach continue its descend below the OCA?
options: When the aircraft has the control tower in sight
When the aircraft is in visual contact with the ground and with the runway lights in sight
When the aircraft is in contact with the ground but not with the runway in sight yet
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Descent below OCA/H requires visual reference with the runway environment or visual approach aids.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: A turn executed by the aircraft during the initial approach between the end of the outbound track and the beginning of the intermediate or final track is a:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: A base turn is executed outbound from a facility to intercept the intermediate/final approach track inbound.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: A manoeuvre in which a turn is made away from a designated track followed by a turn in the opposite direction to permit the aircraft to intercept and proceed along the reciprocal of the designated track is called a:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: This describes a standard procedure turn maneuver (e.g., 45°/225° or 80°/260°).
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question:
You are on an IFR flight executing a circling approach. A descend below the MDA should not be made until:
1 the pilot has the landing threshold in sight
2 visual reference has been established and can be maintained
3 the required obstacle clearance can be maintained and a landing can be made
The combination regrouping all the correct statements is:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: All three criteria must be fulfilled to descend below MDA during a circling approach.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: In an offset entry into an omni directional racetrack procedure, the time on the 30° offset track is limited to:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: The maximum time spent on the 30° offset leg during a entry procedure is 1 minute.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: In an approach procedure, a descent or climb conducted in a holding pattern is called:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: A shuttle is defined as a climb or descent maneuver executed within a holding pattern.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Which are the phases of a missed approach procedure?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: A missed approach procedure consists of three distinct phases: initial, intermediate, and final.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: When determining the OCA for a precision approach, obstacle height is referenced to:
options: highest obstacle within 25 nm of aerodrome
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Obstacle Clearance Height (OCH) for precision approaches is referenced to the threshold elevation.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What is gradient for departure runway?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: The standard instrument departure climb gradient requirement is 3.3%.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: The ILS glide path is normally intercepted between:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Glide path interception typically occurs between 3 NM and 10 NM from the threshold.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: The factors considered in the calculations of DA / DH are:
options: The OCA/H based on the highest obstacle in the final approach path only, plus a margin for height loss on any go around
The OCA]H based on the highest obstacle in the missed approach path only plus an allowance for height loss on any go around
The OCA/H based on the highest obstacle in the approach or missed approach paths including an allowance for aircraft speed and height loss on any go around, plus a margin for operational factors
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: DA/DH calculations combine OCA/H for approach and missed approach paths, aircraft speed, height loss during go-around, and operational margins.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What is the obstacle clearance in the intermediate approach segment?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Minimum obstacle clearance in the primary area of the intermediate approach segment is 150 m (492 ft) or 300 m depending on sub-segment criteria.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Who is establishing the aerodrome operational minima for instrument approaches?
options: The appropriate authority of the State of the aircraft operator
The appropriate authority of the State of the aerodrome
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: The air operator establishes operating minima for its flights, subject to approval by the State of the Operator.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What is the primary area during the intermediate section of an instrument approach?
options: 3/4 of the total width of the airspace used to determine the minimum obstacle clearance for the approach
1/2 of the total width of the airspace used to determine the minimum obstacle clearance for the approach
10 NM either side of the approach path
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: The primary area comprises the central 1/2 (50%) of the total width of the approach corridor.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: In relation to the three entry sectors, the entry into the holding pattern shall be according to:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Holding entry sector selection is determined based on heading relative to the entry sector boundaries.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Related to the three entry sectors in a holding pattern, there is a zone of flexibility on either side of the sectors boundaries of:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: A 5° flexibility zone is permitted on either side of sector boundaries.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What is the outbound timing in a holding pattern above FL 140?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Outbound timing for holding is 1 minute at or below FL140, and 1.5 minutes (90 seconds) above FL140.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: In a holding pattern all turns are to be made at a:
options: Rate of 3°/sec or at a bank angle of 25°, which ever requires the lesser bank
Rate of 3°/sec or at a bank angle of 20°, which ever requires the lesser bank
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Holding pattern turns must be executed at 3°/sec (Rate 1) or 25° bank angle, whichever requires the lesser bank.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: In a standard holding pattern turns are made:
options: In a direction depending on the wind direction
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: A standard holding pattern uses right-hand turns.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What is the rate of turn/bank angle required for turns in a holding pattern?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Standard turn rate in holding is 3 degrees per second.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: What obstacle clearance is guaranteed at a range of 5 nm from the edge of the holding area?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Obstacle clearance reduces in the buffer area and drops to nil beyond the secondary buffer boundary.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: An expected approach time is given:
options: When an aircraft is instructed to hold
Once an aircraft has been holding for 20 minutes
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: An Expected Approach Time (EAT) is issued whenever delay in holding is anticipated.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: When you are asked to hold on a non standard holding fix (eg en route) what direction are the turns made?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Unless specifically published or instructed otherwise by ATC, all holding patterns default to standard right-hand turns.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Standard airway holding pattern below 14 000 ft ?
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Standard holding patterns below 14,000 ft utilize right-hand turns and a 1-minute outbound leg.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Type B instrument app operations with DH below 100 feet and RVR below 300 meters are classified as:
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: Operations with DH < 100 ft and RVR < 300 m correspond to Category III operations.
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.question: Purpose of VSS is to?
options: Visual Safety Surface purpose is to identify obstacles that may affect the execution of an instrument approach procedure (except a circling approach).
Visual Segment Surface purpose is to identify obstacles that may affect the execution of an instrument approach procedure (except a circling approach).
Visual Safety Surface purpose is to identify obstacles that may affect the execution of an instrument approach procedure (including a circling approach)
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.explanation: The Visual Segment Surface (VSS) protects the visual segment of an instrument approach procedure (excluding circling).
PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES:.chapter: PROCEDURES FOR AIR NAVIGATION SERVICES: AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS

NATIONAL LAW.question: A pilot can fly an aircraft which is not entered in the aircraft rating of his licence for endorsement on his licence
options: With in 5 nm of an aerodrome
With in Local Flying Area of the aerodrome
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: As per Indian Aircraft Rules, a pilot training for a new aircraft rating endorsement is permitted to fly within the local flying area of the aerodrome under supervision/approval.

NATIONAL LAW.question: A pilot can fly in 30 consecutive days
options: 100 hrs PIC & 50 hrs as Co pilot
100 hrs PIC & 30 hrs as co pilot
120 hrs PIC & 20 hrs as co pilot
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: According to DGCA flight time limitations, flight time in any 30 consecutive days is capped at 100 hours PIC / 125 total hours with specified limits on co-pilot hours.

NATIONAL LAW.question: When an aircraft is being refueled, the refueling must be stopped if a jet aircraft crosses with in a distance of:
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Refueling operations must cease if a jet aircraft operates or taxis within 43 meters (150 feet) of the refueling zone due to jet blast and ignition risks.

NATIONAL LAW.question: Mathura Refinery is a:
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Mathura Refinery is designated as a Prohibited Area (VA-P) for civil aviation flights in Indian airspace.

NATIONAL LAW.question: A passenger visited a yellow fever infected area on the previous six days, but is not in possession of valid yellow fever certificate, then action taken is:
options: Referral of suspect travellers to designated quarantine facility by Airport Health Organisation.
Immigration Officer to hand over the suspect to District Health Officer.
DGCA to order an inquiry against the Airline for carrying such passenger.
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Under Indian Indian Public Health Regulations, passengers arriving from yellow fever endemic areas without valid vaccination certificates are referred to Airport Health Organisation quarantine facilities.

NATIONAL LAW.question: Prisoners on Board an aircraft can be carried with the permission of
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Carriage of prisoners onboard civil commercial flights requires explicit authorization from the Director General of Civil Aviation (DGCA).

NATIONAL LAW.question: Smoking on a private aircraft is permitted:
options: Provided the owner has no objection.
Only if the certificate of airworthiness of the aircraft permits.
Without restriction if no passengers are carried.
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Smoking on board an aircraft is strictly prohibited unless specifically permitted by the Certificate of Airworthiness.

NATIONAL LAW.question: An aircraft without registration markings can be flown only
options: If the sale deed is not yet completed
For purpose of test flight only, prior to purchase.
If specially permitted in writing by the central govt.
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: No aircraft shall fly in India without registration markings unless special exemption in writing is granted by the Central Government/DGCA.

NATIONAL LAW.question: The member of operating crew shall not have taken alcoholic drinks:
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: DGCA Civil Aviation Requirements state flight crew members must not consume alcohol within 12 hours prior to flight commencement.

NATIONAL LAW.question: Photography at an aerodrome can be done with prior permission in writing from :
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Photography at defense or civil aerodromes is prohibited unless permitted in writing by the DGCA / Central Authority.

NATIONAL LAW.question: While refueling is in progress, no naked light be brought within
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Safety regulations mandate that no naked light or source of ignition be brought within 30 meters (100 feet) of the aircraft or refueling equipment.

NATIONAL LAW.question: A pilot flying low due to thunder showers for safety reasons can be sued by:
options: Owner of the property over which it is flying.
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Under the Aircraft Act, no action for trespass or nuisance lies in respect of flight conducted at reasonable height or for safety/weather necessity.

NATIONAL LAW.question: A person can bring to India human remains of a person:
options: Subject to Public health clearance of Dead bodies/human remains.
After properly cremating human remains only ashes can be brought enclosed in a sealed urn.
Only if these are carried by a Cargo/chartered aircraft.
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Carriage of human remains into India is subject to mandatory Public Health Clearance issued at the port of entry.

NATIONAL LAW.question: An aerial work aircraft on a IFR plan to Jaipur departs at 1032 hrs UTC. Sunset time at Jaipur is 1318 UTC. Night landing facilities are not available at Jaipur. The flying time available to him to reach Jaipur is :
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: 13:18 UTC - 10:32 UTC = 2 hours and 46 minutes (or up to published twilight/sunset limits).

NATIONAL LAW.question: Minimum crew required on private aircraft is:
options: As specified in the certificate of the Airworthiness
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Minimum flight crew requirements are governed by the Type Certificate / Certificate of Airworthiness of the specific aircraft.

NATIONAL LAW.question: Responsibility for implementing International Health Regulations (IHR), 2005 at Indian Airports is that of:
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) under Ministry of Health implements IHR requirements across Indian points of entry.

NATIONAL LAW.question: Dropping of paper leaf lets require the permission of:
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Dropping articles or leaflets over inhabited areas requires authorization from local administration / District Magistrate and DGCA.

NATIONAL LAW.question: A certificate of registration is valid from the date of registration to.
options: Till the aircraft is destroyed in an accident
Till it is cancelled by DGCA
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: A Certificate of Registration (CoR) issued by DGCA remains valid continuously until suspended or cancelled by the authority.

NATIONAL LAW.question: The provisions contained in the Aircraft Rules, 1937 shall:
options: Apply to all unmanned aircraft systems.
Apply to only unmanned aircraft systems weighing more than 500 Kgs, excluding Defence systems.
Not apply to the Unmanned Aircraft Systems except for those specifically provided in these rules.
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: General provisions of Aircraft Rules 1937 do not apply to UAS except where specifically explicitly applied, as UAS are governed by Drone Rules.

NATIONAL LAW.question: If your aircraft is carrying cargo for remuneration, it will be known as a:
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: An aircraft used for transporting passengers or cargo for hire, reward, or remuneration is classified as a Public Transport aircraft.

NATIONAL LAW.question: One pilot will be designated as PIC of a public transport aircraft for each flight by:
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: The air transport operator designates the Pilot-in-Command (PIC) for every scheduled/non-scheduled public transport flight.

NATIONAL LAW.question: The privileges of a license can be exercised by a pilot involved in an incident after:
options: He is cleared by the medical authority
He is cleared by the DGCA
He is cleared by the ATS authority
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Following an aviation incident/accident, pilot privileges remain suspended pending official investigation and clearance by DGCA.

NATIONAL LAW.question: No of cabin crew is required according to
options: No. of passengers excluding crew members
No. of persons on board including crew members
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Cabin crew requirement (e.g. 1 per 50 seats) is calculated based on passenger seating capacity/configuration of the aircraft.

NATIONAL LAW.question: Succession of command is given:
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: The order and rules for succession of command among flight crew members are published in the company's Operations Manual.

NATIONAL LAW.question: An international flight from India can take off:
options: from any major aerodrome in India.
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Flights departing India for international destinations must depart exclusively from designated Customs Aerodromes.

NATIONAL LAW.question: PIC of an aeroplane shall
options: Be responsible for safe conduct of navigation
Be responsible for safe conduct of flight at all times
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: The Pilot-in-Command is directly responsible for, and is the final authority as to, the operation and safety of the aircraft.

NATIONAL LAW.question: An a/c with seating capacity of 150, what is the number of flight attendants required to be carried on the flight:
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Rule requires 1 cabin crew for every 50 passenger seats (or fraction thereof). For 150 seats: 150 / 50 = 3 flight attendants.

NATIONAL LAW.question: Every member of the Flight Crew shall get his log book certified for correctness by the competent authority;
options: At the end of each calendar month
At the end of every quarter
At an half yearly interval ending Jun and Dec.
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Flight crew logbooks must be presented for verification and certified by competent authorities quarterly.

NATIONAL LAW.question: If a passenger falls sick on board an a/c and he is suspected of any infectious disease then PIC's action is:
options: To inform health officer of destination aerodrome.
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: In case of suspected infectious diseases onboard, the PIC must notify Airport Health Officer/ATC prior to landing at destination.

NATIONAL LAW.question: The Pilot-in-Command may permit the access of internet services by passengers on board an aircraft in flight, through Wi-Fi on board, provided:
options: The manufacturer has certified the aircraft for usage of Internet service and the devices used by passengers are kept on flight mode.
The aircraft is certified by DGCA for usage of wifi and is flying in VMC weather conditions and pilot is in contact with ground.
The Director-General has certified the aircraft for usage of Internet service in flight through Wi-Fi on board.
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: In-flight Wi-Fi internet access in Indian airspace requires certification by the Director-General of Civil Aviation.

NATIONAL LAW.question: If any person contravenes any of the provisions of Indian aircraft Act or the rules made thereunder:
options: The licence, certificate or approval issued to such person may be suspended or cancelled.
The person may be arrested and will not be eligible for bail.
the person may be imprisoned for up to one year or fined Rupees one crore in lieu.
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Contravention of Aircraft Act or Rules provides power to DGCA to suspend, revoke, or cancel relevant licenses, certificates, or approvals.

NATIONAL LAW.question: No authorized person must be present within _____ mts of a/c while refueling is on
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Unauthorized persons must remain at least 15 meters away from the aircraft and refueling equipment during aircraft fueling operations.

NATIONAL LAW.question: Pilots log book is to be preserved for
options: 5 years from the date of starting the log book
5 years from the date of last entry
3 yrs from the date of last entry
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Logbooks must be preserved for a minimum of 5 years following the date of the final recorded entry.

NATIONAL LAW.question: Medical for a CPL holder is valid for
options: 1 year if age is less than 40 years
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: Class 1 medical fitness for CPL holders under 40 years of age is valid for 12 months (1 year).

NATIONAL LAW.question: Operational Manual is:
options: Prepared by the operator and authorized by the DGCA
Prepared by the DGCA and authorized by operator
Prepared by the operator and authorized by manufacturer
NATIONAL LAW.explanation: The Operations Manual is drafted by the air operator and submitted to DGCA for official review and approval.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: An applicant for an Airline Transport Pilot Licence shall have completed in aeroplanes not less than:
options: 100 hours of instrument time, of which not more than 50 hours may be instrument ground time
150 hours of instrument time, of which not more than 75 hours may be instrument ground time
100 hours of instrument time, of which not more than 30 hours may be instrument ground time
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: As per ICAO Annex 1 and DGCA CAR Section 7, ATPL requirements specify 100 hours of instrument time, of which maximum 50 hours may be instrument ground time.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: The holder of a pilot's licence should inform the Authority of any illness which they are suffering which involves incapacity to undertake those functions to which the licence relates throughout a period of a certain number of days or more. The number of days is:
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: A licence holder must inform the licensing authority in writing of any illness/injury causing incapacity for 15 days or more.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: The International Civil Aviation Convention Annex containing standards and recommended practices for Personnel Licensing is:
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: ICAO Annex 1 contains Standards and Recommended Practices for Personnel Licensing.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: The holder of a commercial pilot licence, when acting as copilot of an aircraft required to be operated with a copilot, shall be entitled to be credit with not more than:
options: 40% of the copilot flight time towards the total flight time required for a higher grade of a pilot licence
50% of the copilot flight time towards the total flight time required for renewal of a commercial pilot licence
100 hours of flying time required for a higher grade of a pilot licence
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: A co-pilot is entitled to credit 50% of co-pilot flight time towards the total flight time required for a higher grade pilot licence (e.g., ATPL).

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: The minimum age of obtaining a PPL is:
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: Under Aircraft Rules 1937 and ICAO Annex 1, the minimum age for the issue of a Private Pilot Licence (PPL) is 17 years.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: The privileges of the holder of a Commercial Pilot Licence-aeroplane shall be:
options: to act as pilot-in-command in any aeroplane engaged in commercial air transportation
to act as pilot-in-command in any aeroplane certificate for single pilot operation other than in commercial air transportation
to act as Pilot-in-command of any aeroplane having an all-up-weight not exceeding five thousand seven hundred Kgs. and which is entered in the aircraft rating of his licence
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: CPL holders can act as PIC of any aeroplane with maximum certified take-off weight (AUW) up to 5,700 kg entered on their licence.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: The duration of the period of currency of a medical assessment shall begin on the date:
options: the license is issued or renewed
reckoned from the date of medical examination
the license is delivered to the pilot
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: The validity period of a Medical Assessment is calculated starting from the date the medical examination is performed.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: Type ratings shall be established
options: for any type of aircraft whenever considered necessary by the authority
only aircraft certificated for operation with a minimum crew of at least two pilots
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: Type ratings are mandated for aircraft requiring a minimum crew of two pilots, high-performance single-pilot aircraft, or whenever deemed necessary by DGCA/authority.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: The holder of a commercial pilot licence when as Co-Pilot performing under the supervision of a pilot who fulfills the flying experience requirements of a check pilot, the duties and functions of a pilot-in-command shall be entitled to be credited:
options: in full with his flight time but not more than 300 hours towards the total time required for a higher grade of pilot licence
50% of the flight time towards the total time required for higher grade of pilot licence in accordance with the requirements of the licensing authority
in full with his flight time towards the total time required for higher grade of pilot licence
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: When performing Pilot-in-Command Under Supervision (PICUS), flight time is credited in full (100%) towards the flight time required for a higher licence.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: An applicant holding a private or commercial pilot license aeroplane for the issue of an instrument rating, shall have completed....hours of cross-country flight time as pilot-in-command of aircraft in categories acceptable to the licensing Authority
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: An applicant for an Instrument Rating (IR) must have completed at least 50 hours of cross-country flight time as Pilot-in-Command (PIC).

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: An applicant for an Airline Transport Pilot Licence shall have completed in aeroplanes not less than:
options: 75 hours of night flight as pilot-in-command or as copilot
100 hours of night flight as pilot-in-command or as copilot
100 hours of night flight only as pilot-in-command
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: ATPL aeronautical experience requirements state a minimum of 100 hours of night flight as PIC or co-pilot.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: For Commercial Pilot Licence aeroplane the applicant shall have completed in aeroplanes not less than if the privileges of the licence are to be expected at:
options: 5 hours Of night flight time including 3 take-offs and 3 landings as pilot-in-command
5 hours of night flight time including 5 take-offs and 5 landings as pilot-in-command
5 hours of night flight time including 10 take-offs and IO landings as pilot-in-command
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: Night flying requirements for CPL include 5 hours of night flight time including 10 take-offs and 10 landings carried out as PIC.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: An applicant for a Commercial Pilot License aeroplane shall have completed in aeroplanes not less than:
options: 150 hours of flight time and 100 hours as pilot-in-command
200 hours of flight time and 70 hours as pilot-in-command
200 hours of flight time and 100 hours as pilot-in-command
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: CPL issuance mandates a minimum of 200 hours total flight time, including at least 100 hours as Pilot-in-Command.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: An applicant for a Commercial Pilot Licence shall have completed in aeroplanes not less than:
options: 20 hours of instrument instruction time of which not more than 10 hours may be instrument ground time
20 hours of instrument instruction time of which not more than 5 hours may be instrument ground time
not less than ten hours of instrument time of which not more than five hours may be on an approved simulator
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: CPL applicants require at least 10 hours of instrument time, of which maximum 5 hours may be conducted on an approved simulator.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: When the holders of aircraft transport pilot licenses aeroplane and helicopter have passed their 40th birthday the medical examination shall be reduced to:
options: 6 months for single crew commercial operations
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: Under ICAO Annex 1 / DGCA rules, after reaching age 40, Class 1 medical validity is reduced to 6 months for pilots engaged in single-crew commercial air transport operations.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: The applicant to exercise the functions of an Instrumental Flight Rating in aeroplanes shall prove, according to ANNEX 1, PERSONNEL LICENSING, his/her capability to pilot such aircraft only by instrumental rules and an engine
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: For multi-engine Instrument Rating privileges, the practical test requires demonstrating competence under IFR with one engine inoperative or simulated inoperative.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: The applicant for an Airline Transport Pilot License shall have completed in aeroplanes not less than ....hours of cross-country flight time, including not less than . ... hours of flight time by night as Pilot-in-Command or as Co-Pilot performing, under the supervision of a pilot who fulfills the flying experience requirements of a check pilot, the duties and functions of a pilot-in-command.
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: ATPL requirement specifies at least 200 hours of cross-country flight time, including not less than 50 hours of night cross-country flight time.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: An applicant for a Commercial Pilot Licence-aeroplane shall have completed not less than....hours of cross country flight time as pilot-in-command including a cross country flight totaling not less than.... km(....NM), in the course of which full stop landings at two different aerodromes shall be made. The hours and distance referred are:
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: CPL requires 20 hours cross-country flight time as PIC including a cross-country flight of at least 540 km (300 NM) with full-stop landings at two different aerodromes.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: An applicant for a Commercial Pilot Licence shall hold a current
options: class medical assessment as prescribed by the state issuing the licence
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: Commercial Pilot Licence (CPL) applicants and holders must maintain a valid Class 1 Medical Assessment.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: The age of an applicant for a Commercial Pilot Licence shall not be less than:
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: Under Aircraft Rules 1937 and ICAO Annex 1, the minimum age to be issued a Commercial Pilot Licence is 18 years.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: To be able to execute a public transport flight, the minimum and maximum age (with ATPL) is:
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: Minimum age for ATPL issuance is 21 years, and upper age limit for commercial public transport flights is 65 years.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: Which of the following Annexes to the Chicago convention contains minimum specifications for a crew licence to have international validity?
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: ICAO Annex 1 (Personnel Licensing) sets international minimum requirements for flight crew licenses.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: An applicant for the—licences shall have the ability to speak and understand the English language used for radiotelepohony communications to the level of proficiency specified by the Director General.
options: PPL, CPL, ATPL, Fit Navigator and Fit Engg
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: English Language Proficiency (ELP) regulations apply to flight crew licenses including PPL, CPL, ATPL, Flight Navigator, and Flight Engineer.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: The privileges of the holder of a Private Pilot's Licence shall be to act as
options: Pilot-in-command or as Co-pilot Of any aeroplane provided no passengers are carried
Pilot-in -command or as Co-pilot of any aeroplane and carry passengers therein with out remunerations
Pilot-in -command or as Co-pilot of any aeroplane employed on aerial work for remuneration
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: PPL holders may act as PIC/Co-pilot carrying passengers provided no remuneration or financial gain is received.

PERSONAL LICENSING.question: If the age of a CPL holder flying a single pilot helicopter for charters is more than 40 years the validity of medical is for
options: 12 months if he is not carrying VIPs
PERSONAL LICENSING.explanation: For commercial single-pilot air transport operations (including single-pilot charter helicopters), Class 1 medical validity reduces to 6 months after age 40.

AIRWORTHINESS OF AIRCRAFT.question: The continuing airworthiness of an aircraft, according to ICAO Annex 8, shall be determined by:
AIRWORTHINESS OF AIRCRAFT.explanation: According to ICAO Annex 8, the State of Registry is responsible for determining the continuing airworthiness of an aircraft.

AIRWORTHINESS OF AIRCRAFT.question: According to ICAO Annex 8, a certificate of airworthiness shall be renewed or shall remain valid subject to the:
options: Laws of the state of registry and operation
Laws of the state of registry
AIRWORTHINESS OF AIRCRAFT.explanation: ICAO Annex 8 specifies that a Certificate of Airworthiness shall be renewed or remain valid subject to the laws of the State of Registry.

AIRWORTHINESS OF AIRCRAFT.question: The technical standards dealing with certification of aeroplanes are at present limited to multi engine aircraft of:
options: Up to 5700Kg maximum certificated take-off and landing mass
Up to 5700Kg maximum certificated take-off mass
AIRWORTHINESS OF AIRCRAFT.explanation: The airworthiness technical standards under ICAO Annex 8 (Part IIIB/IV) primarily apply to multi-engine aeroplanes of over 5,700 kg maximum certificated take-off mass.
