AIRWORTHINESS OF AIRCRAFT.question: When an aircraft has sustained damage, the aircraft shall be allowed to resume its flight, if
options: The state of registry, the state of design and the state of manufacture consider that the aircraft is still airworthy
The state of manufacture informs the state of registry that the damage sustained is of a nature such that the aircraft is still airworthy
The state of registry considers that the damage sustained is of a nature such that the aircraft is still airworthy
AIRWORTHINESS OF AIRCRAFT.explanation: When an aircraft sustains damage, it is up to the State of Registry to judge whether the damage is of such a nature that the aircraft is still airworthy to resume flight.

AIRWORTHINESS OF AIRCRAFT.question: Jet Airways flight is to take off from London to Bosnia. C of A will be as per the rules of:
AIRWORTHINESS OF AIRCRAFT.explanation: Because Jet Airways is registered in India, the Certificate of Airworthiness (C of A) regulations are governed by the State of Registry (India).

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: Flight Duty Period and Flight Time Limit for 2 crew international scheduled flight is ___ hrs, ___ hrs and ___ landings.
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: According to DGCA flight time limitations, the max FDP and flight time for a 2-pilot international scheduled flight configuration is 11 hours FDP, 8 hours flight time, and 6 landings.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: Route guides are required to be carried in
options: Aircraft involved in scheduled transport services
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: Indian Aircraft Rules specify that route guides and relevant navigation documentation must be carried on board all aircraft operated on flights.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: The duty time of the trainee pilot:
options: Is calculated as per the Flight Time And Flight Duty Period Limit
Is not affected by the Flight Duty Period and Flight Time Limit
Is the time calculated from take off to landing
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: Trainee pilots performing flight duty or operating crew duties fall within the scope of Flight Time and Flight Duty Period (FDP) limitations.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: A pilot can fly in 28 consecutive days
options: 100 hrs PIC & 50 hrs as co pilot
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: DGCA Flight Time Limitations restrict total flight time for flight crew to a maximum of 100 hours in any 28 or 30 consecutive days.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: Flight Manual is to be carried by
options: If C of A states so
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: Every Indian aircraft is required to carry the official Flight Manual or approved equivalent documents on board during flight operations.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: A pvt. Aircraft from Chennai to Colombo is required to carry on board.
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: International flights by private aircraft must carry mandatory documents including Journey Log Book, Route Guide, C of A, C of R, and relevant licenses.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: The maximum duty time limit per day extension for a scheduled flight is
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: In unforeseen operational circumstances, the maximum permissible FDP extension granted to PIC for scheduled operations is 2 hours.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: Max flying hours for a flight crew in 90 consecutive days is:
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: DGCA Flight Time Limitations cap total flight hours for flight crew members at 300 hours in any 90 consecutive days.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: With regard to flight time limitations, "flight time" means:
options: The total time from when an aircraft first moves under its own power for the purpose of taking off until it comes to rest after the flight
The time between take-off and landing
The time between an aircraft starting to move and coming to a complete stop plus one and a half hours
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: Flight time (block time) is defined as the total duration from when an aircraft moves under its own power for taking off until it comes to rest at the end of the flight.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: The maximum permitted flight time for flight crew is :
options: 81 hours in the 27 days prior to the flight
120 hours in the 27 days before the current flight
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: The maximum cumulative flight time allowed for flight crew under DGCA CAR regulations is 1000 hours in 365 consecutive days (1 calendar year).

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: A flight to be operated with a pressurized aeroplane will not be commenced unless a sufficient quantity of stored breathing oxygen is carried to supply;
options: All crew members and passengers, when the atmospheric pressure in any compartment occupied by them is less then 700 hPa
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: Pressurized aircraft must carry supplemental breathing oxygen for occupants whenever cabin pressure drops below 700 hPa (approx. 10,000 ft cabin altitude).

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: Emergency and cockpit check list is to be carried by
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: An emergency and normal cockpit checklist must be maintained and accessible on board all aircraft during operations.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: Number of first aid kits to be carried on board an aircraft carrying 250 passengers is:
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: For aircraft configured with 201 to 300 passenger seats, DGCA CAR requires 3 First Aid Kits to be carried on board.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: No person, other than a flight crew member assigned to a flight, is admitted to or carried in, the flight deck unless that person is:
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: Flight deck access is restricted to assigned flight crew, operating crew members, or persons authorized under regulatory security rules.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: Low Visibility Procedures (LVP) procedures are applied at an aerodrome for the purpose of ensuring safe operations during
options: Category I, Category II and III approaches
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: Low Visibility Procedures (LVP) are implemented at aerodromes to support CAT II/III precision approaches and Low Visibility Take-Offs (LVTO).

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: For an unplanned event, such as unforecast weather, equipment malfunction, or air traffic delay that is beyond the control of the operator 'Flight Time' and 'Flight Duty Period' for scheduled operations may be extended as follows:
options: Flight Time by maximum of 2 hours and FDP by maximum of 4 hours subject to a cumulative limit of maximum of 8 hours and maximum of 16 hours respectively in 30 consecutive days.
Flight Time by maximum of 4 hours and FDP by maximum of 8 hours.
Flight Time by maximum of 1 hour and FDP by maximum of 2 hours
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: Unplanned extensions allowed for scheduled operations due to unexpected delays permit a maximum extension of 1 hour for Flight Time and 2 hours for FDP.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: Minimum trip fuel required shall be the amount of fuel required to enable the aeroplane to fly from take-off or the point of in-flight re-planning,
options: until landing at the destination aerodrome taking into account the operating conditions.
until overhead at the destination aerodrome taking into account the conditions.
until over head at the destination aerodrome taking into account the fuel required to go to a diversion.
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: Trip fuel is defined as the exact fuel quantity required from take-off/re-planning until landing at the destination aerodrome considering operational factors.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: Scheduled operators may be authorized LVTO minima of up to:
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: Depending on airfield infrastructure and operator certification, Low Visibility Take-Off (LVTO) minima can be approved down to 125 meters RVR.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: If, after commencing an instrument approach, the reported RVR/Visibility falls below the applicable minimum, the approach shall not be continued:
options: below AOM published for the aerodrome.
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: Under the approach ban policy, if reported RVR drops below minima before crossing 1,000 ft above aerodrome elevation, the approach must not be continued below 1,000 ft.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: All FDRs shall be capable of retaining the information recorded during at least the last ____ hours of their operation. CVRs atleast ____ hrs and Data link recorders shall be capable of retaining the information recorded during at least the last ____ hours of their operation.
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: Standard recorder requirements specify Flight Data Recorders (FDR) retain at least 25 hours, CVRs retain 2 hours, and Data Link Recorders retain 2 hours.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: Filed minima is 300 m. Touch down zone RVR is 400 m. Relevant mid-point RVR is 100m and stop-end RVR 300m. The runway is:
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: Because a relevant required zone (mid-point RVR = 100m) is below the required minimum (300m), the overall runway condition is considered below minima.

OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.question: CARS is a:
OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES.explanation: In flight recorder terminology (CAR/CARS), it refers to Lightweight Airborne Recording Systems / Cockpit Audio Recording Systems.

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: MMEL is drawn up by:
options: The operator and approved by the certification authority
The manufacturer and approved by the DGCA
The operator from a main list drawn up by the manufacturer
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: The Master Minimum Equipment List (MMEL) is established by the aircraft manufacturer and approved by the state certification authority.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The Minimum Equipment List (MEL) is established by:
options: The aeronautical authority the airline operator depends on
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: The MEL is established by the operator based on the MMEL and approved by their local aviation authority.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: A piece of equipment on your public transport airplane fails while you are still parked. The reference document you use in the first place to decide on the procedure to follow is:
options: The operation manual's chapter "Abnormal and Emergency Procedures"
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Prior to take-off, equipment unserviceabilities are evaluated using the Minimum Equipment List (MEL) to determine dispatch capability.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The minimum equipment list of a public transport airplane is to be found in the:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: The MEL is part of the operator's Operations Manual (OM Part B/System Manuals).
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: In public transport, prior take-off in icing conditions, the captain must check that:
options: External surfaces are free from any ice accretion which may impede the airplane performance and manoeuvrability, except within the limits specified by the flight manual
External surfaces are free from any ice accretion greater than 5mm
Possible ice accretions do not cause to exceed weight and balance limits
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Clean Aircraft Concept mandates critical external surfaces remain clean of ice, frost, and snow except within limits specified in the Flight Manual.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The accumulation of snow or ice on an aircraft in flight induces an increase in the:
options: Value of the stall angle of attack
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Ice/snow accumulation disrupts airflow, decreases maximum lift coefficient, and increases stalling speed.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Which of the following requirements should be met when planning a flight in icing conditions:
options: The flight should be planned so that a change of cruising level can be initiated rapidly
The aircraft shall before flight sprayed with anti-icing fluid
The aircraft shall be equipped with approved ice-protection systems
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Flights into known or expected icing conditions require an aircraft equipped with approved anti-icing or de-icing equipment.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: You are the captain of a commercial airplane and you notice, after take-off, a flock of birds which may present a bird strike hazard, you must:
options: Immediately inform the appropriate ground station
Draft a bird strike hazard report upon arrival and within at most 48 hours
Inform the appropriate ground station within a reasonable period of time
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Immediate notification to ATS allows ground controllers to alert other aircraft to potential bird strike hazards.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: What is the most effective method for scaring birds?
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Pyrotechnic shell crackers are recognized as one of the most immediate and effective active deterrents for dispersing birds.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: 90% of bird strikes occur:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Statistically, over 90% of bird strikes occur below 500 m (approx. 1,500 ft AGL) during take-off, approach, and landing.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The observations and studies conducted on the behaviour of birds on the ground, ahead of an aircraft taking off and having reached an average speed of 135 kt, show that birds fly away:
options: From the beginning of the takeoff roll.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Studies show birds tend to react late to high-speed approaching aircraft, usually scattering only about 2 seconds before arrival.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Who has the responsibility for establishing operating procedures for noise abatement purposes during instrument flight in compliance with ICAO PANS OPS:
options: State in which the aeroplane is operating
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: The operator establishes noise abatement departure/arrival procedures in accordance with ICAO guidelines and local requirements.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: About procedures for noise attenuation during landing:
options: Such procedures will not involve the prohibition of using reverse thrust
They prohibit the use of reverse thrust
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Noise abatement landing procedures do not prevent or prohibit safety-critical systems like reverse thrust when required for stopping distance.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
Noise abatement shall not be the determining factor in the designation of a runway, under the following circumstances:
1. when cross wind component, including gust, exceeds 15kt
2. when the tailwind component, including gust, exceeds 5 kt
3. when the runway is not clear or dry
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Noise abatement preferential runways must not be selected if adverse crosswinds (>15 kt), tailwinds (>5 kt), or contaminated runway conditions exist.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: In accordance with (ICAO) DOC 8168 - OPS, noise preferential routes are established to ensure that departing and arriving aeroplanes avoid over flying noise-sensitive areas in the vicinity of the aerodrome as far as practicable. In establishing noise preferential routes:
options: No turns should be required coincident with a reduction of power associated with a noise abatement procedure.
Turns during take-off and climb should not be required unless the bank angle for turns is limited to 28° (climbing at V2 + 10 to 20 Kt).
Turns during take-off and climb should not be required unless the aeroplane has reached and can maintain throughout the turn a height of no less than 100 m above terrain and the highest obstacle.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: ICAO PANS-OPS states turns should not coincide with thrust reductions during noise abatement procedures to maintain control margins.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: What precludes a runway being used for noise abatement procedures if landing in VMC?
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Preferential noise abatement runways require appropriate instrument or visual guidance systems (e.g., ILS or visual glide slope indicators).
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: During an approach procedure which involves noise abatement, the aeroplane is to be in the final landing configuration at any point after passing the ____ a point from the threshold of the landing runway, whichever is earlier.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Under noise abatement procedures, final landing configuration should be established by the outer marker or 5 NM from threshold, whichever is earlier.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: In case of an engine nozzle fire while on ground you:
options: Pull the fire shut off handle and trigger the engines fire-extinguisher
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Tailpipe/nozzle fires on the ground are typically purged by dry cranking (motoring) the engine with fuel OFF.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
To extinguish a fire in the cockpit, you use:
1. A water fire-extinguisher
2. A powder or chemical fire-extinguisher
3. A halon fire-extinguisher
4. A C02 fire-extinguisher
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Halon and CO2 extinguishers are suitable for flight deck/cockpit electrical and general fires without causing corrosive or obstructive residue.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
You will use a C02 fire-extinguisher for:
1. A paper fire
2. A plastic fire
3. A hydrocarbon fire
4. An electrical fire
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: CO2 extinguishers are rated for Class B (hydrocarbon/flammable liquid) and Class C/Electrical source fires.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
You will use a dry chemical powder fire-extinguisher for:
1. A paper fire
2. A plastic fire
3. A hydrocarbon fire
4. An electrical fire
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Dry chemical powder extinguishers are multipurpose and effective across Class A, B, and electrical fires.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
C02 type extinguishers are fit to fight:
1. Class A fires
2. Class B fires
3. Electrical source fires
4. Special fires: metals, gas, chemical product
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: CO2 extinguishers are designed specifically for liquid fuel (Class B) and electrical equipment fires.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: To fight a fire in an air-conditioned cargo hold:
options: You turn off the cargo hold ventilation and extinguish fire
Fire-fighting is not necessary, since the transport of combustible goods in an air-conditioned cargo hold is forbidden
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Turning off ventilation deprives the fire of oxygen and prevents smoke recirculation into occupied areas before agent discharge.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
In case of a fire due to the heating of the brakes, you fight the fire using:
1. A dry powder fire extinguisher
2. A water spray atomizer
3. A water fire-extinguisher
4. A C02 fire-extinguisher to the maximum
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Hot brake fires are extinguished using dry powder or water fog/mist atomizers to cool without causing explosive thermal shock.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: A class A fire is a fire of:
options: Solid material, generally of organic nature
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Class A fires involve ordinary solid combustible materials such as wood, paper, textiles, and plastics.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: After landing, in case of high temperature of the brakes you:
options: Release the parking brake and you approach the wheels sidewards
Release the parking brake and you approach the wheels either from aft or fore
Apply the parking brake and approach the wheels sidewards
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Overheated wheels must be approached from front or rear (fore or aft) because thermal deflation/explosion projects rim fragments sideways.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: H20 extinguishers are fit to fight:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Water (H2O) fire extinguishers are suitable exclusively for Class A solid material fires.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
The fire-extinguisher types which may be used on Class B fires are:
1. H20
2. C02
3. Dry-chemical
4. Halogen
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: CO2, dry chemical, and Halon (halogenated hydrocarbons) are all effective and approved for Class B liquid fires.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
The fire-extinguisher types which may be used on Class A fires are:
1. H20
2. C02
3. Dry-chemical
4. Halogen
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Class A fires can be fought with H2O, dry chemical, or Halon extinguishers.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
A dry-chemical type fire extinguisher is fit to fight:
1. Class A fires
2. Class B fires
3. Electrical source fires
4. Special fires: metals, gas, chemicals
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Standard dry chemical extinguishers cover Class A, Class B, and electrical source fires.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: A fire occurs in a wheel and immediate action is required to extinguish it. The safest extinguishant to use is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Dry powder is the preferred agent for wheel assembly and brake fires as it avoids thermal shock explosion risks.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: To use passengers oxygen in case of severe cabin smoke is:
options: Useless because breathing oxygen would explode under smoke conditions
Useless because the toxic cabin smoke is mixed with the breathing oxygen
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Passenger drop-down masks mix ambient cabin air with oxygen, allowing toxic smoke to be inhaled.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Following a heavy mass landing on a short runway, you should check the:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Heavy landings require intense braking, making brake temperatures a primary concern for potential fire or thermal fuse plug release.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The correct statement about extinguishing agents on board aeroplanes is:
options: Water may only be used for minor fires
Burning cargo in cargo-aeroplanes is usually extinguished by using carbon dioxide
Halon is an effective extinguishing agent for use in aeroplanes
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Halon is widely utilized in aviation due to high effectiveness per weight unit and leaves no chemical residue.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: If smoke appears in the air conditioning, the first action to take is to:
options: Determine which system is causing the smoke
Put on the mask and goggles
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: The initial emergency response to cockpit smoke is Donning Oxygen Masks and Protective Goggles (100% emergency oxygen).
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Beneath fire extinguishers the following equipment for the fire fighting is on board:
options: A hydraulic winch and a big box of tools
A big bunch of fire extinguishing blankets
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Crash axes or crowbars are carried on aircraft to facilitate access to hidden fires behind cabin panels or linings.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: A class B fire is a fire of:
options: Solid material usually of organic nature
Special fire: metal, gas, chemical product
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Class B fires involve flammable liquids or liquefiable solids like fuels, oils, and solvents.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Fire fighting in the toilets must be performed with:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Standard procedures recommend discharging hand fire extinguishers and supplementing with non-flammable cabin liquids if necessary for Class A waste compartment fires.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The system which must be switched off in case of a belly compartment fire is generally the:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Cargo compartment ventilation is isolated/shut off to starvation-kill the fire and confine extinguishing agent.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
You will use a water fire-extinguisher (straight jet) on a fire of:
1. Solid (fabric, carpet, ...)
2. Liquids (ether, gasoline, ...)
3. Gas
4. Metals (sodium, ...)
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Straight stream water extinguishers are restricted strictly to Class A solid materials.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
You will use a halon extinguisher for a fire of:
1. Solids (fabric, plastic, ...)
2. Liquids (alcohol, gasoline, ...)
3. Gas
4. Metals (aluminium, magnesium, ...)
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Halon is effective against Class A solids, Class B liquids, and Class C flammable gas/electrical fires.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: An engine fire warning will switch on the relevant fire shut-off-handle. The fire shut-off-handle will be switched off when:
options: The fire shut-off handle has been pulled
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Engine fire warning lights cancel/turn off as soon as the detection loops register that temperature drops below threshold.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
A 1211 halon fire-extinguisher can be used for:
1. A paper fire
2. A fabric fire
3. An electric fire
4. A wood fire
5. A hydrocarbon fire
The combination Of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Halon 1211 (BCF) can be used across paper, fabric, electrical, wood, and liquid hydrocarbon fires.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
A C02 fire extinguisher can be used for:
1. A paper fire
2. A hydrocarbon fire
3. A fabric fire
4. An electrical fire
5. A wood fire
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: CO2 extinguishers are rated for liquid fuel (hydrocarbon) and electrical fires.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
A water fire-extinguisher can be used without restriction for:
1. A paper fire
2. A hydrocarbon fire
3. A fabric fire
4. An electrical fire
5. A wood fire
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Water extinguishers can be used without restriction on solid Class A materials: paper, fabric, and wood.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: After a landing, with overweight and over speed conditions, the tyres and brakes are extremely hot. The fireguards should approach the landing gear tyres:
options: Only from left or right sides
Only from front or rear side
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Approach hot landing gear components exclusively from the fore or aft to avoid injury from sideways tire/wheel rim fragment explosions.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
For a flight deck fire which of the following do you use?
1. Halon.
2. Dry Powder.
3. Water.
4. BCE
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Halon and dry chemical/powder extinguishers are preferred for cockpit/flight deck fire emergencies.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: An aircraft is configured for seating 61 to 200 passengers. What is the requirement for hand held fire extinguishers.
options: 4 conveniently located in the passenger compartment.
2 conveniently located in the passenger compartment.
3 conveniently located in the passenger compartment.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: For seating capacity of 61 to 200 passengers, regulations require at least 3 hand-held fire extinguishers located in the passenger cabin.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The number of hand fire extinguishers which must be conveniently located in the passenger compartment when the maximum approved passenger seating configuration is between 401 and 500 is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: For passenger seating configurations between 401 and 500, regulations mandate 6 hand fire extinguishers in the passenger compartment.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Water fire extinguisher with a directed spray can be used on which fires?
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Water spray extinguishers are intended for Class A solid organic fuel fires.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
You will use a Halon extinguisher for a fire of:
1. Solids (fabric, plastic, ...)
2. Liquids (alcohol, gasoline, ...)
3. Gas
4. Metals (aluminium, magnesium, ...)
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Halon extinguishes Class A, B, and C fires but is generally ineffective or hazardous on Class D combustible metals.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Fire extinguishers should be located in the pilots compartment and...
options: At each passenger compartment that is separate from the pilots compartment and not readily accessible to the flight crew.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Mandatory placement requires extinguishers in flight deck and in separate passenger compartments not readily accessible to flight crew.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: In case of an engine jet pipe fire while on the ground you:
options: Carry out a wet motoring cycle.
Carry out a dry motoring cycle.
Pull the fire shut off handle and trigger the engines fire extinguishers.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Engine tailpipe/jet pipe fires are handled by dry motoring the engine to blow out unburnt fuel.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: If cabin altitude increases during level flight, the differential pressure:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Differential pressure is ambient pressure minus cabin pressure. As cabin altitude climbs (cabin pressure decreases), differential pressure drops.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The minimum requirements for Supplemental Oxygen to be supplied in pressurised aeroplanes during and following an emergency descent are that for pilots it shall be available for the entire flight time that the cabin pressure altitude exceeds a minimum of X feet. That minimum of X feet is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Flight crew oxygen must be available continuously when cabin pressure altitude exceeds 13,000 ft.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: A slow decompression may be caused by:
options: a leak in a door seal during normal pressurised flight
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Minor defects like door seal degradation result in slow pressurization loss.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: When flying in straight and level flight at FL290 for some considerable time a small leak develops in the cabin which causes a slow depressurisation, this can be seen on the cabin rate of climb indicator which will indicate:
options: A rate of descent of approximately 300fpm
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: As cabin pressure decreases, cabin altitude increases, shown as a positive rate of climb on the cabin VSI.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: An aeroplane suffers an explosive decompression at an altitude of 31000ft. What is the initial action by the operating crew?
options: Place the seat belts signs to ON
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Immediate survival action upon rapid depressurization at high altitude is donning oxygen masks set to 100%.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
A slow decompression may be caused by:
1 a cracked window
2 a bad functioning of the pressurization
3 a minor leak in the fuselage
4 the loss of a door
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Window cracks, outflow valve control issues, or minor fuselage seal leaks cause slow depressurization, whereas loss of a door causes rapid/explosive depressurization.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
A fast decompression is recognizeable by the following elements:
1. Mist in the cabin
2. Blast towards the exterior of the aircraft
3. Expansion of body gases
4. Blast of air released violently from the lungs
combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Rapid depressurization causes condensation mist, high airflow towards leaks, expansion of trapped gases, and forced lung exhalation.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Supplemental oxygen is used to:
options: provide people on board with oxygen during a cabin depressurisation
protect a crew who fights a fire
assist a passenger with breathing disorders
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Supplemental oxygen systems supply passengers and crew following loss of cabin pressurization.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Oxygen should be used after rapid decompression in an emergency descent until what altitude?
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Emergency descent continues until reaching a safe altitude where supplementary oxygen is no longer required (10,000 ft or MEA).
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
In case of an unexpected encounter with windshear, you will:
1. set the maximum take-off thrust
2. increase the pitch-up attitude up to the limit actuating the stick shaker
3. pull in the drag devices (gear and flaps)
4. keep the airplane's current configuration
5. try to reach the maximum lift-to-drag ratio
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Windshear escape maneuver mandates applying TOGA/max thrust, rotating to pitch limits near stick shaker, and maintaining configuration until clear.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
If you encounter a "microburst" just after taking-off, at the beginning you will have:
1. A head wind
2. A strong rear wind
3. Better climb performances
4. A diminution of climb gradient
5. An important thrust drop
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Initial penetration of a microburst outflow produces an increasing headwind and temporary performance surge before entering downdraft and tailwind.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
During a landing approach, the aircraft is subjected to windshear with an increasing tailwind. In the absence of a pilot action, the aircraft:
1. flies above the glide path
2. flies below the glide path
3. has an increasing true airspeed
4. has a decreasing true airspeed
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: An increasing tailwind reduces IAS/TAS and causes loss of lift, dropping the aircraft below the glide path.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Wind shear may be described as a change in wind direction and/or speed in space, including up draughts and downdraughts. To counter the effects of windshear the amount of control action that is required is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Severe windshear response requires immediate, aggressive, and substantial flight control and power inputs.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: While approaching the outer-marker, the tower informs you about the presence of a "microburst". You will expect to encounter:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Microbursts generate localized severe vertical downdrafts and rapidly shifting horizontal windshear.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: One Of the main characteristics Of windshear is that it:
options: Occurs only at a low altitude (2000ft) and never in the horizontal plane
Can occur at any altitude in both the vertical and horizontal planes
Can occur at any altitude and only in the horizontal plane
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Windshear occurs at all altitudes, manifesting as vertical shifts, horizontal speed changes, or both.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Which one of the following magnitudes will be the first to change its value when penetrating a wind shear?
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Air mass speed changes instantly affect IAS before aircraft inertia changes groundspeed or flight path.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: An aircraft which experiences a headwind of 40kt while making its way towards the centre of a microburst may expect, when crossing the microburst, to face a tailwind of:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Traversing symmetrical microburst outflow from a 40 kt headwind across to the opposite outflow results in an 80 kt total wind change to tailwind.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: When a commercial transport passenger airplane is equipped with a door in the flight crew compartment area, this door must include:
options: A locking system to prevent any unauthorized access
A sealing system allowing the maintenance for as long as possible of the pressure in the cockpit in case of a depressurization in the compartment area
Distinctive red or yellow colored markings indicating the access area (in cae of a blocked door)
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Flight deck doors on commercial aircraft must be lockable from within to prevent unauthorized entry.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: In addition to inform each State, whose citizens are known to be on board aircraft, the State of the country in which an aircraft has landed after an act of unlawful interference must immediately notify the:
options: State of Registry of the aircraft, the State of the operator and ICAO
State of Registry of the aircraft and the State of the operator only
State of Registry of the aircraft and the DGCA
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: ICAO Annex 17 mandates immediate notification to the State of Registry, State of Operator, and ICAO.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: In case of a hi-jack, the squawk code is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Transponder code 7500 signifies unlawful interference/hijacking.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The flight deck door should be capable of being:
options: Remotely locked from either inside or outside the compartment
Remotely locked by cabin crew operation from outside the compartment
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Security standards require flight deck doors to be lockable from the pilot workstation inside the cockpit.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Who has the responsibility to take adequate measures for the safety Of passengers and crew of an aircraft which is subjected to an act of unlawful interference until their journey can be continued? The:
options: Contracting State in which the unlawful interference occurs
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: The Contracting State where the aircraft lands or is located holds safety responsibility for passengers and crew.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Following an act of unlawful interference on board an aeroplane, to whom the commander should submit a report of the act to:
options: Both the local authority and the Authority of the State of the operator
The Authority of the State within which the aeroplane is operating at the time of the unlawful interference
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: The commander must submit a detailed report to both local host authorities and their home State of Operator authority.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: When flight crew members are at their duty stations they must:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Operating flight crew must keep seat belts/harnesses fastened at assigned stations.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: In addition to informing each State, whose citizens are known to be on board an aircraft, the State of the country in which an aircraft has landed after an act of unlawful interference must immediately notify the:
options: State of Registry of the aircraft, the State of the operator and ICAO.
State of Registry of the aircraft and the State of the operator only.
State of the operator, the J.A.A. and ICAO.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Under Annex 17, notifications must reach State of Registry, State of Operator, and ICAO.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
In case of ditching, the cabin attendants will:
1. evacuate women and children first
2. have the passengers embark directly in the life rafts
3. prevent passenger movements which may impede the airplane's flotation ability
4. ensure the complete evacuation of the airplane
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Standard ditching procedures instruct boarding life rafts directly from aircraft doors and restricting uncoordinated movements.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Mist in the cabin, pressure and temperature drop characterize:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Rapid pressure drop leads to adiabatic expansion, sudden temperature drop, and condensation fog/mist.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: In the event of a precautionary landing, who is responsible for alerting the rescue services?
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Air Traffic Control (ATC) alerts emergency and rescue services upon receiving emergency or precautionary notifications.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: If ditching is inevitable:
options: Passengers should be briefed that even if they successfully evacuate aeroplane it is inevitable that some of them will die from drowning.
The use of life jackets is to be reiterated before the ditching.
Life jackets are to be inflated before leaving the aeroplane.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: In an impending ditching, cabin crew reiterate life jacket donning instructions; life jackets are inflated only when exiting.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
From the following list:
1. Fuel jettisoning system and its operation are free from fire hazard
2. The fuel discharges clear of any part of the aeroplane
3. Fuel fumes do not enter any part of the aeroplane
4. The jettison operation does not adversely affect the controllability of the aeroplane
Which of the above are requirements that must be shown to exist during fuel jettisoning tests:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Certification flight tests ensure discharged fuel remains clear of structure and fumes do not re-enter fuselage compartments.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Fuel Jettison should be carried out:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Fuel jettisoning guidelines recommend altitude above 6,000 ft AGL over unpopulated areas, but emergency overriding conditions allow jettisoning anywhere when safety dictates.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Fuel Jettison:
options: May be ordered by ATC to reduce aeroplane mass in an emergency situation.
Is a procedure to reduce mass in an emergency only.
Is a procedure that may be employed to reduce aeroplane mass where an overweight landing may result in damage to the aeroplane.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Fuel jettisoning is strictly an emergency procedure initiated by the pilot-in-command to reduce aircraft landing mass.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: A list of dangerous goods, which may not be transported by air, can be found in:
options: The shipper's declaration for dangerous goods
The technical instructions for the safe transport of dangerous goods by air
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: ICAO Technical Instructions (Doc 9284) detail forbidden items and transport conditions for dangerous goods.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: In compliance with the CAR-OPS, in order to carry hazardous materials on board a public transport airplane, they must be accompanied with a:
options: Representative of the company owning the materials
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Dangerous goods shipments require a formal Dangerous Goods Transport Document (Shipper's Declaration).
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The general information, instructions and recommendations on the transport of hazardous materials are specified in the:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Operational instructions and dangerous goods handling policies for flight crews are contained in the operator's Operations Manual.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Products or materials are considered to be dangerous goods if the products or materials in question are defined as such by:
options: The IATA document entitled "Regulations governing the transportation of dangerous goods by air"
The directive of the Community Union
The ICAO document entitled "Technical Instructions for the safe transportation of dangerous goods by air"
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: ICAO Technical Instructions for Safe Transport of Dangerous Goods by Air is the legally binding international standard.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: ICAO Appendix 18 is a document dealing with:
options: The air transport of live animals
The safety of the air transport of hazardous materials
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: ICAO Annex 18 establishes international standards for Safe Transport of Dangerous Goods by Air.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The dangerous goods transport document, if required, shall be drawn up by:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: The shipper who originates the dangerous goods shipment is legally responsible for preparing and signing the Dangerous Goods Transport Document.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Can dangerous goods be carried in the passenger cabin or on the flight deck?
options: Yes, provided they are non toxic.
Yes, if authorised by the authority.
Yes, but only goods specified in the technical instructions
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Only specific exempted dangerous goods listed in Technical Instructions (e.g., medical items, small passenger carry-ons) are permitted in cabin/cockpit.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Your flight manual does not include specific supplementary information on landing distances on wet runways and the service bulletins or weather reports indicate that the runway may be wet at the estimated time of arrival. The required landing distance on a dry runway must be increased by:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Standard performance regulations require adding at least 15% to the dry landing distance for wet runway conditions.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: A runway is considered damp when:
options: Its surface is not dry, and when surface moisture does not give a shiny appearance
It is covered with a film of water of less than 3mm
Surface moisture gives it a shiny appearance
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Damp describes a surface that is not dry but where surface moisture is insufficient to produce a reflective/shiny appearance.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question:
A runway is considered wet when:
1. It is covered with a quantity of water or loose or slushy snow less than or equal to the equivalent of 3mm of water
2. The amount of surface moisture is sufficient to modify its colour but does not give it a shiny appearance
3. The amount of surface moisture is sufficient to make it reflective, but does not create large stagnant sheets of water
4. It bears stagnant sheets of water
The combination of correct statements is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: A wet runway status applies when moisture makes the surface reflective (up to 3 mm water depth) without forming large standing pools.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The presence of dynamic hydroplaning depends primarily on the:
options: Depth of the standing water of the runway
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Dynamic hydroplaning occurs when water depth exceeds tire tread depth, lifting the tire off the pavement.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The braking efficiency is a piece of information presenting itself in the form of a:
options: Letter falling between A and E
Combination of the terms: poor, medium, good
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Braking action reports are categorized using descriptive terms such as Good, Medium, Poor, or Unreliable.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: A runway covered with 4 mm thick water, is said to be:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Standing water depth greater than 3 mm classifies the runway surface as contaminated.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: A runway is considered damp when:
options: It is covered with a film of water of less than 1 mm.
Its surface is not dry, and when surface moisture does not give it a shiny appearance
It is covered with a film of water of less than 3 mm.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Damp condition definition requires non-dry surface without shiny/reflective water sheen.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The effect whereby a tyre is lifted from the runway due to aeroplane speed along the runway is known as:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Hydroplaning (aquaplaning) occurs when fluid pressure lifts a rotating tire from the runway surface.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Viscous hydroplaning is caused by:
options: A smooth and dirty runway surface.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Viscous hydroplaning occurs on smooth, wet, or contaminated (oil/rubber deposits) surfaces at lower speeds.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: What is the shortest distance in a sequence for landing between a "Heavy" aircraft preceeding a "Light" aircraft
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: ICAO wake turbulence radar separation distance for Light following Heavy on approach is 6 NM.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: A separation minimum shall be applied between a LIGHT or MEDIUM aircraft and a HEAVY aircraft and between a LIGHT aircraft and a MEDIUM aircraft when the heavier aircraft is making a low or missed approach and the lighter aircraft is landing on the same runway in the opposite direction or on a parallel opposite direction runway separated by:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Standard ICAO opposite direction threshold/parallel runway distance criteria for wake turbulence application is less than 760 m.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: A separation minimum shall be applied between a LIGHT or MEDIUM aircraft and a HEAVY aircraft and between a LIGHT aircraft and a MEDIUM aircraft when the heavier aircraft is making a low or missed approach and the lighter utilizing an opposite direction runway for take off, this minimum is:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: The non-radar timed separation minimum for opposite direction operations under low/missed approach conditions is 2 minutes.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: In order to meet the wake turbulence criteria, what minimum separation should be applied when a MEDIUM aircraft is taking off behind a HEAVY aircraft and both are using the same runway?
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Non-radar wake turbulence separation for Medium taking off behind Heavy on the same runway is 2 minutes.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: In order to meet wake turbulence criteria, for arriving aircraft and using timed approaches, what minima shall be applied to aircraft landing behind a heavy or a medium aircraft?
options: Medium aircraft behind other medium aircraft- 2 minutes
Medium aircraft behind heavy aircraft- 3 minutes
Medium aircraft behind heavy aircraft- 2 minutes
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Timed approach minimum for a Medium aircraft landing behind a Heavy aircraft is 2 minutes.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: What is the minimum wake turbulence separation criteria when a LIGHT aircraft is taking off behind a MEDIUM aircraft and both are using the same runway?
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Take-off separation for a Light aircraft behind a Medium aircraft on the same runway is 2 minutes.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: The letter "L" is written in the wake turbulence box of a flightplan form when the maximum certified take-off weight of an aircraft is less than or equal to:
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Light (L) wake turbulence category applies to aircraft with Maximum Certificated Take-off Mass ≤ 7,000 kg.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.question: Wake turbulence risk is highest:
options: If, just before landing a much lighter aircraft has landed at the same runway with heavy crosswind.
When a heavy aircraft has just performed a take-off at a closely situated parallel runway with a light crosswind.
When a preceding aircraft has briefly applied take-off thrust just prior to take off
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.explanation: Light crosswinds can drift dangerous wingtip vortices from heavy aircraft departing on parallel runways directly onto the active takeoff path.
SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZAR.chapter: SPECIAL OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES AND HAZARDS (GENERAL ASPECTS)

COMMUNICATION.question: What does QDR mean?
options: Magnetic heading to the station (no wind)
COMMUNICATION.explanation: QDR is the Q-code representing the magnetic bearing FROM the station.

COMMUNICATION.question: If you are requested to report your height, to which Q-code-setting would you refer?
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Height is defined as vertical distance above a specific datum (usually aerodrome elevation), measured using the QFE altimeter setting.

COMMUNICATION.question: Which Q-code is used to report altitude?
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Altitude is the vertical distance above mean sea level, measured using QNH.

COMMUNICATION.question: What does ATIS mean?
COMMUNICATION.explanation: ATIS stands for Automatic Terminal Information Service.

COMMUNICATION.question: What is the Q-code for "magnetic heading to the station (no wind)"?
COMMUNICATION.explanation: QDM is the magnetic heading required to steer towards a station with no wind.

COMMUNICATION.question: What does CTR mean?
COMMUNICATION.explanation: CTR stands for Control Zone.

COMMUNICATION.question: What is the Q-code for "true bearing from the station"?
COMMUNICATION.explanation: QTE represents the true bearing of the aircraft FROM the station.

COMMUNICATION.question: What is the Q-code for "magnetic bearing from the station"?
COMMUNICATION.explanation: QDR is the magnetic bearing FROM the station.

COMMUNICATION.question: QNH is the Q-code to indicate:
options: The atmospheric pressure referred to the highest obstacle located on the surface of an aerodrome.
The atmospheric pressure measured at the aerodrome reference point (ARP).
The altimeter sub-scale setting to obtain elevation when on the ground.
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Setting QNH on the altimeter subscale makes the instrument display the aerodrome elevation when on the ground.

COMMUNICATION.question: What does QDL mean?
options: I intend to ask you for a series of bearings.
True heading to the station (no wind).
COMMUNICATION.explanation: QDL is the Q-code meaning 'I intend to ask you for a series of bearings'.

COMMUNICATION.question: What does QNE mean?
options: What indication will my altimeter give on landing at .. (place) at hours, my sub-scale being set to 1013.2 millibars (29.92 inches)?
What should I set on the subscale of my altimeter so that the instrument would indicate its height above the reference elevation being used?
What should I set on the subscale of my altimeter so that the instrument indicate its elevation if my aircraft were on the ground at your station?
COMMUNICATION.explanation: QNE is the indication given on landing when the sub-scale is set to standard pressure (1013.2 hPa / 29.92 inHg).

COMMUNICATION.question: A radio direction finding station will use the following Q code to pass a true heading (no wind) to an aircraft to head for that station:
COMMUNICATION.explanation: QDM is the magnetic heading to steer for the station (or true heading when corrected for magnetic variation). In typical multiple-choice options, QDM is used for heading to steer to the station.

COMMUNICATION.question: The order of priority of the following messages in the aeronautical mobile service is:
options: Meteorological message, direction finding message, flight regularity message
Distress message, flight safety message, urgency message
Distress message, urgency message, direction finding message
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Message priorities in order: Distress, Urgency, Direction Finding, Flight Safety, Meteorological, Flight Regularity.

COMMUNICATION.question: What is the correct way of transmitting the number 3500 when indicating an altitude or an height?
COMMUNICATION.explanation: For altitude/height expressed in thousands, hundreds are pronounced: 'Three thousand five hundred'.

COMMUNICATION.question: During the transmission of numbers containing a decimal point:
options: The term Decimal can be omitted if no chance of misunderstandings exists
The term Decimal must always be transmitted
The term Decimal must be spoken only if followed by three digits
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Standard RT phraseology mandates that the term 'DECIMAL' must always be spoken when transmitting numbers containing a decimal point.

COMMUNICATION.question: The time is 9:20 A.M. What is the correct way of transmitting this time if there is no possibility of confusion about the hour?
COMMUNICATION.explanation: When the hour is unambiguous, only the minutes are transmitted using individual digits: 'Two zero'.

COMMUNICATION.question: Which phrase shall be used if you want to say: AN ERROR HAS BEEN MADE IN THIS TRANSMISSION (or message indicated). THE CORRECT VERSION IS:
COMMUNICATION.explanation: The standard phraseology for correcting an error during transmission is 'CORRECTION'.

COMMUNICATION.question: A message preceded by the phrase TRANSMITTING BLIND DUE RECEIVER FAILURE shall be transmitted:
options: On the frequency presently in use.
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Blind transmissions due to receiver failure are made on the frequency currently in use.

COMMUNICATION.question: Which phraseology is to be used to ask the control tower for permission to taxi on a runway in the direction opposite to that in use?
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Standard requesting phraseology to backtrack on the runway is 'Request backtrack on runway'.

COMMUNICATION.question: Which phrase shall be used if you want to say: "Yes"
COMMUNICATION.explanation: In standard aviation radiotelephony phraseology, 'AFFIRM' is used for 'Yes'.

COMMUNICATION.question: The phrase used by ATC to instruct you to listen out on a frequency is:
COMMUNICATION.explanation: 'MONITOR' means listen out on (frequency).

COMMUNICATION.question: What is the radiotelephony call sign for the aeronautical station providing surface movement control of aircraft on the manoeuvring area:
COMMUNICATION.explanation: GROUND provides surface movement control on the manoeuvring area.

COMMUNICATION.question: What is the radiotelephony call sign for the aeronautical station providing approach control radar departures:
COMMUNICATION.explanation: The call sign suffix for approach control radar services is APPROACH RADAR (or RADAR).

COMMUNICATION.question: The initial call from an aircraft, callsign AIR INDIA 285 weighing more than 136 tonnes would be:
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Aircraft with maximum certificated take-off mass of 136,000 kg or more append the word 'HEAVY' immediately after their callsign on initial contact.

COMMUNICATION.question: On the readability scale what does "Readability 3" mean:
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Readability scale: 1 = Unreadable, 2 = Readable now and then, 3 = Readable with difficulty, 4 = Readable, 5 = Perfectly readable.

COMMUNICATION.question: A test call shall not continue for more than:
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Radio test transmissions should not exceed 10 seconds.

COMMUNICATION.question: King air VT-ABC receives the following instruction: "V-BC climb straight ahead until 2500feet before turning right, wind 270 degrees 6 knots, cleared for take-off". What is the correct read back:
options: Straight ahead, 2500 feet right turn, wind west 6 knots, cleared for take-off, v-BC
Straight ahead, at 2500 feet right turn, cleared for take-off, V-BC
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Readbacks must include flight path parameters and takeoff clearances, while non-mandatory items like wind information can be omitted.

COMMUNICATION.question: Which elements of instructions or information shall always be read back?
options: Runway in use, altimeter settings, SSR codes, level instructions, heading/speed instructions
Runway-in-use, visibility, surface wind, heading instructions, altimeter settings
Time check, runway in use, altimeter settings, level instructions, SSR codes
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Mandatory readback elements include runway in use, altimeter settings, transponder codes, level instructions, and heading/speed instructions.

COMMUNICATION.question: When the term "Overcast" is used in an aviation routine weather report (METAR), the amount of clouds covering the sky is:
options: No clouds but poor ground visibility
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Overcast (OVC) means 8 octas cloud coverage (100%).

COMMUNICATION.question: What is the correct way of expressing visibility?
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Visibility in METAR and aviation reports is expressed in metres up to 10 km.

COMMUNICATION.question: When the term "Cavok" is used in an aviation routine weather report (METAR), the values of visibility and clouds are:
options: Visibility 10 km or more, no clouds below 5000 feet/GND
Visibility more than 8 km, no clouds below 3000 feet/GND
Visibility 10 km or more, no clouds below 1500 feet/GND
COMMUNICATION.explanation: CAVOK requires visibility of 10 km or more and no cloud below 5000 ft (or below highest MSA) and no CB/TCU.

COMMUNICATION.question: When the term "Broken" is used in an aviation routine weather report (METAR), the amount of clouds covering the sky is:
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Broken (BKN) represents 5 to 7 octas of cloud cover.

COMMUNICATION.question: When the term "Scattered" is used in an aviation routine weather report (METAR), the amount of clouds covering the sky is:
options: Half or less than half (3 or 4 octas)
More than half but less than overcast (5 to 7 octas)
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Scattered (SCT) represents 3 to 4 octas (half or less than half) cloud cover.

COMMUNICATION.question: An aircraft station fails to establish radio contact with an aeronautical station on the designated frequency. What action is required by the pilot:
options: Return to the airport of departure
Land at the nearest airport without an ATC unit
Attempt to establish contact with the station on an alternative frequency
COMMUNICATION.explanation: When contact fails on the designated frequency, the pilot should attempt contact on alternative frequencies or with other stations.

COMMUNICATION.question: In the event that a pilot is required to make a blind transmission, this should be made:
options: Only once on the designated frequency
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Blind transmissions are transmitted twice on the designated frequency.

COMMUNICATION.question: Distress is defined as:
options: A condition concerning the attitude of an aircraft when intercepting the localizer during an ILS approach
A condition concerning the safety of a person on board or within sight and requiring immediate assistance
A condition of being threatened by serious and/or imminent danger and requiring immediate assistance
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Distress is a condition of being threatened by serious and/or imminent danger requiring immediate assistance.

COMMUNICATION.question: Under which of the following circumstances shall an aircraft squawk 7700?
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Mode A code 7700 is set to select an emergency/distress condition.

COMMUNICATION.question: An aircraft in distress shall send the following signal by radiotelephony:
COMMUNICATION.explanation: The radiotelephony distress signal is MAYDAY spoken three times.

COMMUNICATION.question: The frequency used for the transmission of a "MAYDAY" call shall be:
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Distress messages should initially be made on the frequency currently in use with the ATC unit.

COMMUNICATION.question: An urgency call content is to be as follows:
options: PAN PAN PAN, aircraft identification, the intention of the person in command, heading, height, position.
PAN PAN PAN (on 121.5 MHz), present position, heading aircraft, identification, the intention of the person in command, the identification of the station being called.
PAN PAN PAN (on the frequency in use), name of station addressed, the nature of the urgency condition, the intention of the person in command.
COMMUNICATION.explanation: Urgency call structure: PAN PAN PAN (on current frequency), station addressed, nature of urgency, intention of commander.

COMMUNICATION.question: An "Automatic Terminal Information Service" provides:
options: Information concerning en-route weather phenomena which may effect the safety of aircraft operation
